signals.title: feat(delegation): subagents can fork the parent conversation (port of kimi-code#3007)
signals.text: ## Summary `delegate_task` gains a `fork` parameter: subagents can now start from a one-time snapshot of the parent's conversation instead of a blank context, so work that builds on the current session no longer needs lossy, token-expensive re-briefing. Port of MoonshotAI/kimi-code#3007 (this week's flagship feature in their Agent tool, MIT) adapted to Hermes' delegation architecture. ## Changes - `tools/delegation_fork.py` (new, ~180 LOC): builds the sanitized parent snapshot — - read from the parent's **persisted session transcript** (`get_messages_as_conversation(include_ancestors=True, repair_alternation=True)`), the same durable source the gateway uses for session restore; - parent's system prompt stripped (the child builds its own focused prompt); per-row bookkeeping keys (`_row_id`, `display_kind`, …) removed; deep-copied; - tail trimmed to the last **completed assistant reply**: the in-flight `delegate_task` tool_call (which can never close inside the child), dangling tool results, and the triggering user prompt are removed so role alternation and tool-call adjacency stay wire-valid — mirrors kimi-code's mid-turn trailing-message handling; - capped to `delegation.fork_max_messages` most-recent messages (default 200, floor 10), with post-cut boundary repair; - kickoff goal framed with an inheritance notice (snapshot = parent's reference material, not the child's own actions) — kimi-code's framing, adapted. - `tools/delegate_tool.py`: `fork` kwarg end-to-end (registry handler → `delegate_task` → child attachment → `_run_single_child` seeds via `run_conversation(conversation_history=...)` — the existing gateway-restore parameter, no new injection path). Top-level `fork` is the batch default; per-task `fork` overrides. Missing session DB / empty transcript degrades to a blank-context spawn with a log line. Schema documents the cost trade-off so models keep fork off for independent tasks. - Docs in the same PR: `features/delegation.md` (new "Forked Subagents" section, warning-box update) and `configuration.md` (`delegation.fork_max_messages`). - `tests/tools/test_delegation_fork.py`: 15 tests — tail trimming (dangling call, completed round-trip, trailing user prompt), system/bookkeeping stripping, cap + post-cut repair, deep-copy isolation, degrade paths (no DB, empty history, DB error), schema/signature wiring. ## Validation | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Continue-the-investigation delegation | full manual re-brief in `context` | `fork: true` seeds parent transcript | | Independent tasks | blank context | unchanged (fork defaults off) | | Mid-turn scaffolding in snapshot | n/a | trimmed to last completed assistant reply | | Parent prompt cache | n/a | untouched (parent context never mutated) | Targeted suites: 128 passed (`test_delegation_fork`, `test_delegate`, `test_delegate_summary_budget`, `test_delegate_toolset_scope`, `test_delegate_composite_toolsets`, `test_delegate_control_actions`). E2E through the real `delegate_task` → `_run_single_child` → `run_conversation` chain with a session-DB-backed parent: snapshot seeded, roles `[user, assistant]`, system prompt absent, kickoff prefixed with the inheritance notice. Source: [MoonshotAI/kimi-code#3007](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code/pull/3007) ## Infographic ![Forked subagents schematic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa72c16/oMLgc2x2_WjHFWb0EQunD_m8fpLwu4.png)

signal.title: Desktop boot death-loop: ~/.hermes/.env override=True clobbers HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN injected by the desktop
signal.text: ## Summary The Hermes desktop app (Electron) fails to boot on a machine where `~/.hermes/.env` contains a `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` line. The app gets stuck in an infinite boot loop: spawn backend → backend HTTP-ready → WebSocket handshake 403 → backend killed as "stale" → respawn → repeat. ## Root cause The desktop spawns `hermes serve` and passes a **fresh per-boot** session token to the child via the environment: - `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:10173` and `:10537` — `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN: token` (a freshly minted `crypto.randomBytes(32)` value). On the backend side, `hermes_cli.main` imports `load_hermes_dotenv()` at module-import time (`hermes_cli/main.py:706`). That function loads `~/.hermes/.env` with **`override=True`** (`hermes_cli/env_loader.py:500`): ```python if user_env.exists(): _load_dotenv_with_fallback(user_env, override=True) ``` So if `~/.hermes/.env` contains a `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` line (stale, from any prior session — in the reported case a leftover `hermes-mobile-…` value), dotenv **overwrites** the fresh value the desktop injected into the child env. The server's in-memory `_SESSION_TOKEN` (resolved from env at `hermes_cli/web_server.py:498-502`) then differs from the token the desktop remembers (`spawnToken`). The desktop's boot sequence (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:10648-10661`) resolves the served token (falls back to `spawnToken`), then probes `/api/ws?token=<token>`. Validation is `_ws_auth_reason` → `hmac.compare_digest(token, _SESSION_TOKEN)` (`hermes_cli/web_server.py:15922-15927`). Because the two tokens diverge, the handshake returns **HTTP 403**, the backend is classified as "stale" (`main.ts:10599` `Ignoring stale Hermes backend exit`), SIGTERM'd, and respawned forever. ## Reproduction 1. Put `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN=anything-stale` in `~/.hermes/.env`. 2. Launch the desktop app (or run `hermes serve` with `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN=fresh` in env). 3. Observe: `GET /api/ws?token=fresh` → 403, while `GET /api/ws?token=anything-stale` → 200. Confirmed locally on macOS arm64, source `9d86ac62b41d2b953aafc7d9c1e75711762f68e5`. ## Why it's a footgun / not just "user error" `_clear_known_keys_missing_from_dotenv` (`env_loader.py:114-145`) is deliberately narrow — it only scrubs a small `_PROFILE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS` allowlist. `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` is a value a **parent process** (the desktop shell) explicitly injects into the child's environment; `.env` should not win over an explicit parent-process injection. Any `.env` carrying that key — which is easy to accumulate (mobile sessions, manually-exported shells, copied config) — will silently break the desktop boot with no obvious error to the user. ## Suggested fix (one of) - In `load_hermes_dotenv`, do **not** let `.env` override env vars that were already present and are in an explicit "injected by parent" allowlist (e.g. `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN`, or more generally any key a parent/spawner set). i.e. `override=False` for those keys, or skip them in the dotenv load. - Or: the desktop should write its token to a place the backend reads as authoritative (or not export the key to `.env` at all), so the two can't diverge. ## Workaround (already applied on the affected machine) Remove the stale `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` line from `~/.hermes/.env`. The desktop regenerates the token every boot, so nothing else depends on the on-disk value. After removal the backend boots cleanly (`Hermes backend is ready`). Reported on behalf of a user; verified against source `9d86ac62b41d2b953aafc7d9c1e75711762f68e5`.

signal.title: feat(cron): jobs can pin their own reasoning effort — CLI-only, kept off the model tool schema (salvage #91038)
signal.text: ## Summary Cron jobs can now pin their own reasoning effort (`hermes cron create/edit --reasoning-effort <level>`), overriding both `agent.reasoning_effort` and per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides` at fire time — salvage of #91038 by @victor-kyriazakos, with the model-facing tool-schema arg removed per standing policy (models don't make model-configuration decisions; the only exception is user-defined profile selection). Coatue request: "Luna max and Luna medium are v different" — heavy scheduled analyses at `high`, cheap recurring jobs at `minimal`, same install. ## Changes - `cron/jobs.py`: `_normalize_reasoning_effort()` validates at the store choke point via the canonical `parse_reasoning_effort` grammar; garbage never persists; absent field = byte-identical job record - `cron/scheduler.py`: `_resolve_job_reasoning_config()` — job pin wins over global + per-model config; invalid hand-edited values warn and fall back rather than killing the tick - `hermes_cli/`: `--reasoning-effort` on `cron create` / `cron edit` (empty string clears) - `tools/cronjob_tools.py`: pin is SURFACED in `action=list` output but **not settable** — removed the `reasoning_effort` schema property and dispatch from the contributor's version; a schema-absence test pins the policy - Docs: cron.md + cli-commands.md updated (tool mention removed, policy noted) ## Validation | | Result | |---|---| | `tests/cron/test_cron_reasoning_effort.py` | 30/30 pass | | `tests/cron/` + `tests/tools/test_cronjob_tools.py` | 917 passed, 1 skipped | | Attribution audit | all emails mapped | Authorship preserved: both contributor commits cherry-picked; schema removal as a follow-up commit. Closes #91038. ## Infographic ![Per-Job Reasoning Effort for Cron Jobs](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa72bd5/VfnT7oJvI0tkc5gLJy0ss_ZZ5j720Y.png)

signal.title: fix(gateway): GATEWAY_RELAY_URL env stamp disables direct messaging platforms
signal.text: ## What When `GATEWAY_RELAY_URL` is set in the process environment, the gateway now disables every other enabled **messaging** platform at config-load time. The connector owns all platform connections on such a deployment; a directly-connected adapter in the same process is a second, unmanaged ingress path. ## Why - A direct adapter beside the relay causes duplicate deliveries and split sessions for the same platform conversation. - A direct adapter holds a live outbound socket, which makes `messaging_is_relay_only_or_absent` false and silently disarms scale-to-zero on managed instances. ## Behavior | Configuration | Result | |---|---| | `GATEWAY_RELAY_URL` env + platform auto-enabled by credentials | platform disabled, INFO log | | `GATEWAY_RELAY_URL` env + platform `enabled: true` in config.yaml | platform disabled, WARNING log that names the platform | | `GATEWAY_RELAY_URL` env + `local` / `api_server` / `webhook` | untouched (same non-messaging exclusion set as the scale-to-zero arm gate) | | `gateway.relay_url` in config.yaml only (no env stamp) | old additive behavior — relay runs beside direct adapters | No escape hatch: the env stamp is a managed-deploy marker, and the mechanism stays minimal until a real mixed-ingress case appears. ## Ops notes - Managed/NAS containers already receive `GATEWAY_RELAY_URL` as a deploy stamp; after this change they cannot accidentally dial Discord/Telegram directly when a stray bot token is present in the container env. - Self-hosted deployments that intentionally mix relay + direct adapters must configure the relay via `gateway.relay_url` in config.yaml instead of the env var. ## Placement The sweep runs at the end of `_apply_env_overrides`, after every enablement pass (YAML, env bridges, plugin `is_connected` probes, relay enablement) and before the `_enabled_explicit` marker cleanup — so it catches credential-auto-enabled platforms and can still distinguish explicit from automatic enablement for log severity. ## Validation - `./scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_config.py` — 58 passed, 0 failed (includes the 2 new tests below). - `./scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/relay tests/gateway/test_scale_to_zero.py tests/gateway/test_scale_to_zero_watcher.py` — 41 files, 281 passed, 0 failed. New tests: - `test_relay_env_url_disables_other_messaging_platforms` — env stamp + explicit telegram + `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` in env: telegram and discord end up disabled, relay and api_server stay enabled. - `test_relay_yaml_url_keeps_other_platforms_enabled` — YAML-only relay config: telegram stays enabled. Not exercised end-to-end: a live connector deployment (this change is config-load only; the connect loop and scale-to-zero arm gate consume the same `enabled` flags they already read).

signal.title: feat(desktop): optional on-device dictation via a loopback Whisper server
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds an **opt-in on-device dictation path** to Hermes Desktop, so push-to-talk transcription can run on the user's own machine instead of travelling to the backend. **Why.** `transcribeAudio()` always uploads the clip to `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. When the desktop app is connected to a **remote backend** (a VPS, an SSH profile, or cloud), that means every dictation recording leaves the machine, crosses the network, and comes back as text. Two costs follow from that: - **Privacy** — your voice is on the wire and on the remote host for the duration of the request, even though the microphone, the audio, and (usually) a perfectly good local Whisper are all right here. - **Latency** — the round-trip, not the transcription, sets the floor. An M-series Mac that transcribes in ~1s locally still waits on Mac → VPS → STT → VPS → Mac. The desktop app already captures the audio locally. The missing piece was only *routing* it, so this PR adds a rung in front of the existing call rather than a second STT stack. **Design.** Per `apps/desktop/AGENTS.md` ("Cross everything as an observable ladder"), dictation becomes an ordered ladder with one resolver owning the policy: 1. `voice.dictation.stt: "local"` → POST multipart to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/audio/transcriptions`, 2.5s timeout. 2. Any failure — no server, non-2xx, unparseable body, timeout — falls through to the backend. The fallback is deliberately **silent**. Dictation is a foreground interaction; a toast about a sidecar the user cannot fix mid-recording is noise, not information. A stopped local server means dictation gets slower, never broken. **The default is unchanged.** `voice.dictation.stt` defaults to `"backend"`, and in that mode `transcribeAudio()` returns the same backend call it always did — same profile scope, same body, same payload-derived timeout, called synchronously with nothing awaited in front of it. **No backend change.** `voice.dictation.*` is desktop-owned and round-trips through `PUT /api/config`'s deep merge untouched. Because `/api/config/schema` therefore never declares these keys — and `sectionFieldEntries()` reads "no schema and no value" as "the field does not exist" — the desktop supplies its own schema/default rung for them (`DESKTOP_FIELD_SCHEMA` / `DESKTOP_FIELD_DEFAULTS`). Backend-owned keys are unaffected: `configValue()` still returns `undefined` for anything not desktop-owned. ## Related Issue Fixes #86607 ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## Changes Made - **`apps/desktop/src/lib/local-stt.ts`** (new) — the whole policy in one place: config resolver, the `$localStt` nanostores atom, data-URL → `File` conversion, and the loopback POST. Constants (`LOCAL_STT_DEFAULT_PORT` 8090, `LOCAL_STT_TIMEOUT_MS` 2500, `LOCAL_STT_DEFAULT_MODEL`) are exported so UI copy and behavior cannot drift. - **`apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts`** — `transcribeAudio()` becomes the ladder; the backend call moves into `backendTranscribeAudio()` verbatim. - **`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-hermes-config.ts`** — seeds `$localStt` alongside the other voice prefs on mount/refresh, so the transcribe path can read it synchronously. - **`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/`** — three rows in Settings → Voice: the route (select), and the port + model, which appear only in `local` mode (`voiceFieldVisible`). Adds `configValue()` so an unset desktop-owned key paints its effective default instead of a blank that reads as "off". - **`apps/desktop/src/i18n/{ar,ja,zh,zh-hant}.ts`** — labels and descriptions for the three new rows in every locale. - **`apps/desktop/src/types/hermes.ts`** — `voice.dictation` and `stt.language` on `HermesConfig`. - **`website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`** — a "On-device dictation" subsection under Voice, tied to the remote-backend section. - **Tests** — `lib/local-stt.test.ts` (16) and the dictation-routing block in `hermes.test.ts` (5), plus additions to `helpers.test.ts`, `voice-field-visible.test.ts`, `voice-provider-fields.test.ts`. ### Config keys | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `voice.dictation.stt` | `backend` | `backend` (unchanged) or `local` | | `voice.dictation.local_stt_port` | `8090` | loopback port of the Whisper server | | `voice.dictation.local_stt_model` | `whisper-1` | `model` part in the upload | The language hint reuses the existing global `stt.language` rather than inventing a fourth key. All three are hardened against hand-edited config: a port arriving as `"9000"` is accepted, a port of `0`/`65536`/`"abc"` falls back to the default, and a blank model resolves to `whisper-1` instead of sending an empty part. `local_stt_model` exists because the two server families disagree: whisper.cpp's `whisper-server` and faster-whisper-server ignore the `model` part and use whatever they loaded, while model-routing servers (speaches, LocalAI) dispatch on it and 400 without a real id. It is deliberately **not** `stt.local.model` — that key holds a faster-whisper *size* (`"base"`), which a routing server would reject, silently turning every dictation into a fallback. ## How to Test Tested on macOS 15 (Apple Silicon), desktop connected to a remote backend. 1. Start any OpenAI-compatible transcription server on loopback, e.g. ```bash whisper-server -m models/ggml-base.bin --port 8090 ``` 2. `npm run dev` in `apps/desktop`. 3. **Default is untouched** — with no config change, dictate into the composer. DevTools → Network shows the request going to the backend and **no** request to `127.0.0.1`. 4. **Local route** — Settings → Voice → *Dictation Transcription* → `local` (the port and model rows appear). Dictate again: the request goes to `127.0.0.1:8090/v1/audio/transcriptions` and **no** request hits `/api/audio/transcribe`. On a remote backend this is where the latency drop is obvious. 5. **Fallback is invisible** — kill the whisper server and dictate once more. The transcript still arrives, from the backend, with no error, no toast, and no stuck recording state. Restart the server and it returns to the local path with no app restart. 6. **Bad config doesn't brick it** — hand-edit `voice.dictation.local_stt_port` to `0` or `"abc"` in `config.yaml`; dictation keeps working (resolver falls back to 8090). Automated (`apps/desktop`): ``` npm run typecheck # clean npx eslint src/ electron/ # 0 errors (93 pre-existing warnings, same as main; 0 on the changed files) npx vitest run --project ui # 441 files / 4059 tests passing ``` `scripts/run_tests.sh` (the Python suite) was also run. Its failures are pre-existing and environmental — messaging-platform and `acp` modules that need optional extras — and reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout in the same venv. This change contains no Python. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this feature - [x] I've run the Python suite (`scripts/run_tests.sh`) — remaining failures are pre-existing/environmental and reproduce on a clean `origin/main`; this change contains no Python. - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (Apple Silicon) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation — `website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md` - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — **N/A**, see "Deliberately out of scope" below - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact — the path is `fetch` + `FormData` in the renderer, identical on all three platforms; nothing shells out and no path handling is involved. The *server* is the user's to run, and `whisper-server` ships for macOS, Windows, and Linux. - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A ## Deliberately out of scope Flagging these so reviewers can push back rather than discover them: - **`cli-config.yaml.example`** — the file documents backend/CLI config. The existing desktop-only voice keys (`voice.auto_tts`, `voice.max_recording_seconds`, `voice.stop_phrases`, `voice.thinking_sound`) are all absent from it, so adding `voice.dictation.*` there would break that precedent and imply the CLI honors keys it never reads. Documented in `desktop.md` instead. Happy to add it if you'd rather the example file be exhaustive. - **Spawning/managing the Whisper process.** Hermes does not install, launch, or supervise the local server; the user runs it. Bundling a whisper binary or adding a sidecar lifecycle is a much bigger change (model downloads, updates, platform binaries, crash supervision) and does not need to block the routing. - **Suggesting `local` automatically on a remote connection.** `$connection` exposes `mode`/`remoteKind`, so the app *could* nudge remote users toward this. I kept it an explicit opt-in: auto-switching a route that depends on a server the app doesn't manage would degrade dictation for everyone who hasn't installed one. The remote-backend motivation is instead carried in the field description and the docs. Easy to add a hint if the team wants it. - **e2e coverage** (`apps/desktop/e2e`). A meaningful e2e would need a real loopback transcription server plus a microphone permission grant; the interesting behavior here is resolver precedence and failure rungs, which the unit tests cover directly (including the abort path under fake timers). Adding an e2e that mocks the loopback server would mostly assert the mock. - **TTS.** Untouched by design — this issue is dictation only.

signal.title: fix(gateway,cron): split inherited PYTHONPATH before dedupe to prevent exponential growth on restart
signal.text: ## Problem Issue #91222: When a gateway or cron watcher inherits a non-empty `PYTHONPATH`, the inherited value was appended as a **single string element** to the candidate list. `dict.fromkeys` cannot decompose it, so every restart added another full copy. On Windows (pathsep ";") this was especially visible — `PYTHONPATH` doubled on each restart. Example (Windows): - Start: `PYTHONPATH=/hermes;/hermes/venv/Lib/site-packages` - 1st restart: `/hermes;/hermes/venv/Lib/site-packages;/hermes;/hermes/venv/Lib/site-packages` - 2nd restart: keeps doubling... ## Root Cause The inherited `PYTHONPATH` string was appended wholesale: ```python pythonpath = [project_entry, site_entry] if os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH"): pythonpath.append(os.environ["PYTHONPATH"]) # one string, never deduped ``` `dict.fromkeys` deduplicates by whole-element identity. The composite string never equals the individual entries, so it always survives and grows. ## Fix Split the inherited `PYTHONPATH` on `os.pathsep` **before** extending the candidate list. Each path entry then dedupes individually against the fresh entries. ```python pythonpath = [project_entry, site_entry] if os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH"): pythonpath.extend(os.environ["PYTHONPATH"].split(os.pathsep)) os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(dict.fromkeys(pythonpath)) ``` Applied to all three affected sites: - `gateway/run.py::_ensure_windows_gateway_venv_imports` - `gateway/run.py::GatewayRunner._start_detached_restart_helper` - `cron/scheduler.py::_windows_cron_python_invocation` (also adds missing `dict.fromkeys` dedupe) ## Testing - Reproduced the bug locally: confirmed PYTHONPATH doubles each restart on the old code, stays stable on the fixed code. - All related tests pass: `tests/gateway/test_restart_drain.py` (13 passed), `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_restart_loop.py` (131 passed), `tests/hermes_cli/test_spawn_gateway_restart_cooldown.py` (9 passed), `tests/hermes_cli/test_spawn_gateway_restart_reap.py` (2 passed), `tests/cron/test_cron_script.py` (27 passed), `tests/cron/` full suite (805 passed).

signal.title: fix(gateway): bound the hygiene-compression turn-hold so a streaming summary cannot freeze the turn
signal.text: # fix(gateway): bound the hygiene-compression turn-hold so a streaming summary cannot freeze the turn ## Symptom On chat platforms (Telegram, and any transport with a comparable idle-timeout), a large session that crosses the hygiene-compression threshold causes the incoming message to **appear frozen** — no spinner result, no reply — even though the gateway process is perfectly healthy. The turn only recovers when the summary eventually completes or the transport gives up. Reported in the wild as the "Sleeping Machan" / agent-goes-silent-mid-turn failure: tools execute server-side, but the turn's output never reaches the user. ## Root cause (exact line) `gateway/run.py` — session-hygiene block (`if _needs_compress:`). The gateway awaits the compression worker inline on the incoming-message path: ```python _compressed, _ = await asyncio.wait_for( asyncio.shield(_hyg_future), timeout=_slice, ) ``` `_slice` is the **inactivity** budget (`hygiene_timeout_seconds`, default 30s), re-charged from `CompressionCommitFence.seconds_since_progress()` each pass. A summary model that keeps streaming tokens keeps resetting the slice, so the `while True:` extension loop can carry the wait all the way to `hygiene_total_ceiling_seconds` (default **600s**). While the gateway is parked in that `await`, **zero bytes hit the wire**. Telegram's idle-timeout (~30s) severs the connection long before the 600s ceiling, so the user's turn freezes even though compression is proceeding normally. The total ceiling prevents a *truly* degenerate stream, but it does nothing to keep the wait under the transport's much-tighter idle-timeout. ## Fix Add **`hygiene_max_turn_hold_seconds`** (default `10`) — a turn-hold budget bounding the wall-clock the incoming message waits on hygiene compression, independent of the inactivity budget: - The wait slice is capped at the **remaining turn-hold budget**, so the budget is re-evaluated even when a continuously-streaming worker keeps the inactivity slice large (without this, the budget check would only run at slice boundaries — too late). - When the budget is exceeded, the gateway abandons the inline wait and proceeds on the **uncompressed transcript** via the existing timeout path — which already revokes the worker's commit admission (`CompressionCommitFence.revoke_commit_admission`) and defers cleanup. The change is **purely additive** (no existing line removed): it only tightens when the already-hardened abandonment path fires. ### Why this is safe (cache / alternation / data) - **No stale clobbering.** The abandoned worker keeps running detached, but its commit is fenced — `revoke_commit_admission` guarantees `begin_commit` is refused, so when it finishes it **cannot** overwrite turns appended after the wait was abandoned. Role alternation and transcript integrity are preserved. - **Prompt caching untouched.** On the abandoned turn the gateway uses the *original* transcript verbatim — no mutation of past context, no system-prompt rebuild. The compression (when it completes on a later, healthy turn) is the same sanctioned exception it always was. - **Fail-closed.** If anything about the abandoned worker misbehaves, the existing fence/cooldown machinery handles it exactly as a normal timeout. ## Behavior-contract test `test_session_hygiene_turn_hold_budget_abandons_streaming_wait` — a worker that **streams progress continuously** (so the inactivity slice never fires on its own) must: 1. be **abandoned** once the wait exceeds `hygiene_max_turn_hold_seconds`, 2. let the turn **proceed on the uncompressed transcript** (responds well under the 600s ceiling), 3. have its stale commit **fenced** — `archive_and_compact` is never called, no session mutation, role alternation intact, 4. still be cleaned up once the detached worker actually finishes. ## Verification - New regression test: **passes** (turn-hold fires, turn proceeds, stale commit fenced, cleanup runs). - Full `tests/gateway/test_session_hygiene.py` (16) + `test_compress_focus.py` + `test_session_race_guard.py`: **26 passed**. - `ruff check` on changed files: **clean**. - Patch applies cleanly on current `main` (`cf64ca2`). ## Production metric Transport idle-timeout rate while a session is in the hygiene-compression state — must drop to zero. Secondary: P99 turn latency for threshold-crossing turns drops from the 600s ceiling to under `hygiene_max_turn_hold_seconds`. ## Config ```yaml compression: hygiene_max_turn_hold_seconds: 10 # raise if your summary model needs longer + your transport tolerates it ``` Docs updated in `website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md`.

signal.title: fix(desktop): collapse Skills Hub browser by default
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? The Skills & Tools page renders the installed-skills list and the embedded Skills Hub browser (an iframe of the live docs site) stacked in the same vertical space, with the Hub **expanded by default**. On a typical laptop screen this squeezes both into a "half page" — a cramped list on top and a small Hub viewport below. The hub's expand/collapse choice already persists across sessions (it rides `$paneHeightOverride('capabilities-hub')` in the shared pane store, `apps/desktop/src/store/panes.ts`, which is backed by `localStorage`) — the only thing missing was starting from collapsed. This implements option 2 from the issue: "Collapse the embedded Hub by default (remember the hide/show choice across sessions)". The fix reuses a pattern that already exists in this codebase for exactly this purpose — `DetailPane`'s `defaultCollapsed` prop (`apps/desktop/src/app/master-detail.tsx:238-242`) seeds a pane's persisted height to `0` the first time its id has no saved state, then gets out of the way; any later user expand/collapse persists and wins from then on. `EmbeddedHubPicker` gets the same one-time seed for its `capabilities-hub` pane id. Nothing else changes: the resizable sash, the "Browse the full hub" / "Hide the hub browser" toggle, and the update-all action all work exactly as before — only the *default* state when a profile has never touched the pane. ## Related Issue Fixes #90767 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/app/skills/embedded-hub-picker.tsx`: seed the hub pane's persisted height to `0` (collapsed) on first touch, mirroring `DetailPane`'s `defaultCollapsed` pattern. Updated the file's own comments, which explicitly documented "expanded by default" as intentional. - `apps/desktop/src/app/skills/index.test.tsx`: added a test that a never-touched profile sees no hub iframe until it clicks "Browse the full hub" (and that opening it is a real, persisted choice); updated two existing tests that asserted the iframe was live on mount to open the hub explicitly first; added a `beforeEach` reset of the pane store so tests don't leak persisted state into each other. ## How to Test 1. Open Desktop → sidebar → Skills & Tools (Skills tab) as a profile that has never opened this page before. 2. Before: the Hub iframe loads immediately below the installed list, splitting the page in half. 3. After: the installed list gets the full page; a "Browse the full hub" button is shown instead. Clicking it opens the Hub, and that choice persists across tab switches and app restarts, same as before. Automated: `npx vitest run src/app/skills/index.test.tsx src/store/panes.test.ts` ``` Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 26 passed (26) ``` Confirmed the new/updated tests fail without the fix (reverted only `embedded-hub-picker.tsx` to HEAD, source file only, kept the updated tests): ``` Test Files 1 failed (1) Tests 3 failed | 9 passed (12) FAIL hub picker starts collapsed — no iframe until the user opens it FAIL hub picker refuses to reinstall an already-installed skill FAIL mounts the hub iframe lazily and keeps it (hidden) across tab switches ``` Also ran, both clean: - `npx tsc -p . --noEmit` - `npx eslint src/app/skills/embedded-hub-picker.tsx src/app/skills/index.test.tsx` (0 errors; pre-existing `no-restricted-globals` warnings for `document.querySelector`, consistent with the rest of the file) - Broader regression sweep: `npx vitest run src/store/ src/app/skills/` → 94 files / 1051 tests passed ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits - [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've added tests for my changes - [ ] I've tested on my platform — ran in a Linux CI-style sandbox only; not manually verified on Windows (the reporter's OS) or macOS ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] N/A — no docs, config keys, or tool schemas changed --- Note: this PR was prepared with AI assistance (an autonomous coding agent), with the diff, tests, and verification steps reviewed before opening.

signal.title: fix(desktop): right rail dead at boot - self-heal visibility drift and reload a wiped in-flight tree read
signal.text: Fixes #91245 ## Summary Two bounded boot-time self-heals for the right-hand file rail, each routed through an existing recovery path: 1. **controller.tsx - rail visibility drift**: when `$hasWorkspace && $fileBrowserOpen` turn true, let adoption/dock-enforcement settle (`setTimeout 0`), then detect the contradictory states where the toggle reads OPEN but the rail cannot render - pane missing from the tree, right side collapsed, or `files` chrome-hidden - and call `revealTreePane(FILES_PANE_ID)`, the same path a layout reset takes. An explicit Cmd-J collapse writes the toggle false, so deliberate closes are never fought. 2. **use-project-tree.ts - skeleton stuck forever**: react to the tree atom being wiped while a cwd is present. Boot-time connection events (`gatewayScope` change, `beforeConnectionSwitch`) call `resetProjectTreeState()`, which can invalidate a root read that is already in flight; the requestId guard rejects its commit and nothing schedules a retry, so the pane shows `[data-slot="tree-skeleton"]` forever. The new effect keys on `[cwd, state.cwd, state.rootLoading]` and forces exactly one reload 50ms after any wipe-with-active-cwd. Deliberate clears (profile switch, Home) also clear the session cwd, so the guard stays hands-off there; a same-cwd reload across a connection switch is desirable anyway since the filesystem may differ. ## Root causes (details in #91245) - `setTreePaneHidden(false)` only fronts the tab; it never un-collapses a side nor re-adopts a pane that left the tree, so persisted drift between `paneStates.v1`'s `"file-browser":{"open":true}` and `"files":{"open":false}` is never reconciled outside of `resetLayoutTree`. - The requestId guard correctly rejects stale commits, but with no retry path a mid-flight wipe leaves `cwd=''`/`loaded=false` permanently. ## Verification Tested on Windows 11 x64 against current `main`, desktop app rebuilt and run with CDP instrumentation: - Before: right rail absent, or present with `treeitems: 0` + skeleton; console capture shows `commit REJECTED {requestId:2, latestReq:3}` with no retry. - After: same boot sequence logs the self-heal reload; DOM shows `treeitems: 22` (project dirs render), skeleton gone. - Manual `window.hermesDesktop.readDir(cwd)` resolves in both cases, confirming the data layer was never at fault. - Explicit Cmd-J close still persists `"file-browser":{"open":false}` and stays closed across restarts (heal condition requires the toggle true). - `npm run typecheck` exit 0; `npx eslint` on both changed files exit 0. ## Notes - No schema/persistence changes; both heals are runtime-only. - The controller heal intentionally excludes the zone-minimized dimension: minimizing the rail row is a deliberate user gesture, and revealTreePane's un-minimize would fight it.

signal.text: ## Summary Telegram tables no longer degrade to bullet lists when `rich_messages: true` and `rich_drafts: false` — the reporter's exact config (Discord support thread continuation, diagnostics d513af1d). Root cause: that config combo disabled Telegram's native DM draft transport entirely, so finalization depended on upgrading a plain edit-in-place message via `editMessageText.rich_message`; when Telegram rejects the upgrade, the legacy MarkdownV2 formatter permanently converts pipe tables to bullets. Support thread: https://discord.com/channels/1053877538025386074/1540026433072668672 ## Infographic ![Telegram tables stay rich](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa72bda/JJK-KIE0xYjmpCLu8kISq_9Ul3K4lB.png)

signal.title: feat(sessions): group conversations into channel-bindable spaces
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds backend-owned session spaces that group conversations independently of cwd. Spaces can optionally bind to one gateway channel, so inbound sessions are assigned without changing their existing session identity, while Desktop and CLI share the same persisted organization. ### Motivation Projects model code workspaces with a unique primary path, so they cannot represent multiple attention contexts that share one cwd. Users need lightweight session grouping that remains available across CLI, gateway, REST, recovery, and Desktop instead of a renderer-only overlay. ### Behavior - Sessions can be assigned to a named Space or left Unassigned without changing their cwd or project. - A Space can bind to one `platform` and `chat_id`; matching gateway sessions are assigned automatically while retaining the existing gateway session key. - Desktop groups sessions by Space and exposes create/assign actions in the session menu. - CLI and REST clients can list, create, update, delete, and assign Spaces. - Offline recovery preserves both the Space registry and session assignments. - Spaces do not add per-space prompts, memory, skills, or project path semantics. ### Implementation The shared session database owns the Space registry, nullable session assignment, and unique channel binding. Gateway ingest, recovery, CLI, and REST APIs use that shared state. Desktop caches Space data by connection and profile, guards against stale refreshes, and renders backend-owned groups. ## Related Issue Closes #91182 ## Type of Change - [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) ## Changes Made - `hermes_state.py` and `hermes_state_common.py` - persist Spaces, channel bindings, and session assignments with migration-safe schema reconciliation. - `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` - apply channel-bound Spaces to gateway-created and recovered sessions. - `hermes_cli/` - expose Space commands, REST models/routes, and recovery support. - `apps/desktop/src/` - add typed Space APIs, profile/connection-scoped caching, sidebar grouping, and create/assign actions. - `tests/` and `apps/desktop/src/store/session-spaces.test.ts` - cover persistence, gateway behavior, REST, recovery, and renderer cache isolation. ## How to Test 1. Run `hermes sessions space-create Work --platform telegram --chat-id <chat-id>` and confirm `hermes sessions spaces` shows the binding. 2. Start or recover a session for that channel and confirm it retains its normal session id while receiving the Space assignment. 3. Open Desktop, group the sidebar by Space, and create, assign, or unassign a session from its action menu. 4. Automated verification already run on the final committed tip: ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_state/test_session_spaces.py tests/gateway/test_session_api.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_session_spaces.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_recovery.py -q cd apps/desktop npx vitest run src/store/session-spaces.test.ts npm run typecheck ``` Results: 32 Python tests passed, 4 Desktop tests passed, and Desktop typecheck passed. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run the repository test entry on the relevant test files and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation - N/A; CLI help and API types describe the new surface - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys - N/A; no config keys changed - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows - N/A; existing session-store ownership is preserved - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior - N/A; no model tool behavior changed ## Screenshots / Logs N/A; automated backend and Desktop state tests cover the behavior.

signal.title: fix(gateway): skip the auto-TTS voice reply for the desktop platform
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Stops the double auto-TTS playback on the desktop surface. When `voice.auto_tts` is enabled, two independent paths synthesize and play the same reply on the desktop: the gateway's `_send_voice_reply` (calling `text_to_speech_tool` and delivering via `adapter.send_voice`) and the desktop app's `useAutoSpeakReplies` hook (calling `/api/audio/speak` → `playSpeechText`). Neither knows about the other, so every desktop reply plays twice — logs show one "Generating speech" but two "TTS audio saved" entries per reply from two different PIDs (#90297). `_should_send_voice_reply` now returns False for the desktop platform, deferring to the desktop's own hook (the authoritative speaker for that surface — it fires on every reply regardless of mode, and the gateway has no way to know whether the client spoke). This is the issue's first suggested fix; the alternative (teaching the hook to detect an already-spoken gateway message) adds cross-process coordination the simple skip avoids. Every other platform keeps its gateway voice reply unchanged. ## Related Issue Fixes #90297 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `gateway/run.py` — `_should_send_voice_reply` skips `event.source.platform.value == "desktop"` right after the mode check, with the double-synthesis mechanism documented inline (#90297) - `tests/gateway/test_desktop_no_gateway_reply.py` — three regressions: desktop is skipped even when global auto_tts would qualify; desktop is skipped even with an explicit `all` mode for the chat (the hook fires regardless); and Telegram with auto_tts on still gets its gateway voice reply (the skip is desktop-only) ## How to Test 1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_desktop_no_gateway_voice_reply.py -q` — should pass (3 passed) 2. Observed result: on unmodified main (verified via `git stash` control), both desktop tests fail — `_should_send_voice_reply` returns True for the desktop platform and the gateway sends a voice reply the desktop hook will speak again; with this fix both shapes return False 3. signal.title: [Bug] Desktop right rail dead at boot: files pane hidden while toggle reads open, or tree stuck on loading skeleton forever
signal.text: ## Environment - **Hermes version**: v0.20.4 line, git install at current `main` (`76952ba54f`) - **OS**: Windows 11 Pro, x64 - **Surface**: Hermes Desktop (Electron app) - **Layout**: default three-column layout, files pane in the right rail ## Summary Two independent boot-time bugs can leave the right-hand file rail dead in different ways. Both reproduce deterministically on Windows with a restored session that has a project cwd; both currently require a manual workaround (layout preset switch + reset, or restarting until timing happens to win). 1. **Rail invisible, toggle reads open** — `$fileBrowserOpen` says OPEN while the rail renders nothing: the right side is collapsed, or the `files` pane is chrome-hidden (`paneStates.v1` records `"file-browser":{"open":true}` alongside `"files":{"open":false}`), or the pane is missing from the tree. Only a layout-preset switch plus reset fixes it. 2. **Rail shell visible, tree stuck on the loading skeleton forever** — the pane mounts, the project name header renders, but `[data-slot="tree-skeleton"]` never goes away and zero rows appear. ## Root cause 1 — visibility drift never re-syncs At bind time `bindPaneVisibility('files', ...)` calls `setTreePaneHidden('files', true)` because no workspace has arrived yet. When the cwd lands, `setTreePaneHidden(false)` only fronts the tab (`frontPaneInGroup`) — it does not un-collapse a collapsed side nor re-adopt a pane that left the tree. Boot-time dock-enforcement of plugin panes (Bot Mode) can also rewrite the persisted tree mid-boot, so the stored state and the toggle disagree in both directions. Nothing reconciles them afterwards; `resetLayoutTree` is the only path that replays `sideOpeners`. ## Root cause 2 — requestId guard eats an in-flight read, nothing retries Boot sequence observed via CDP console capture: ``` useProjectTree effect: cwd=<project> -> loadRoot(force) starts, requestId=2 <gatewayScope change / beforeConnectionSwitch> -> resetProjectTreeState(), requestId=3 readProjectDir resolves in 18ms with 22 entries commit REJECTED: requestId=2 != latest.requestId=3, latest.cwd="" ``` After the rejection the atom stays cleared (`cwd=''`, `loaded=false`, `rootLoading=false`) while the workspace is active. The load-retry effects key on `connectionKey`/`cwd`/workspace ticks — all already settled by then — so no retry ever fires and the skeleton shows forever. `loadRoot`'s own early-return guard (`current.rootLoading`) also blocks any incidental re-entry. ## Repro 1. Sign in with a session whose cwd points at a real local project. 2. Restart the desktop app. 3. On a slow-enough gateway handshake (or any run where the connection events land after the first root read starts), the right rail either doesn't appear, or appears with an eternal skeleton. 4. `localStorage['hermes.desktop.paneStates.v1']` shows the contradictory `"file-browser":{"open":true}` / `"files":{"open":false}` pair in case 1. Verified live over CDP (`--remote-debugging-port`): `treeitems: 0` with a present skeleton before the fix; manual `window.hermesDesktop.readDir(cwd)` resolves fine in the same session, proving the data layer was healthy and the state machine was the problem. ## Fix (branch pushed, PR incoming) Two small self-heals, each bounded and routed through existing recovery paths: - **controller.tsx**: subscribe to `computed([$hasWorkspace, $fileBrowserOpen])`; when it turns true, let adoption settle (`setTimeout 0`), then if the pane is missing from the tree / side collapsed / pane hidden, call `revealTreePane(FILES_PANE_ID)` — the same path a layout reset takes. An explicit ⌘J close writes the toggle false, so deliberate closes are not fought. - **use-project-tree.ts**: an effect keyed on `[cwd, state.cwd, state.rootLoading]` that forces exactly one reload whenever the tree atom is wiped while a cwd is present. Deliberate clears (profile switch, Home) also clear the session cwd, so the guard stays hands-off there. Related: #79518 (same family — reveal/adoption preserving stale hidden flags), #65173/#65376/#66059 (file-browser toggle state fights around boot).

signal.title: fix(native_compaction): preserve compression summary messages during pre-checkpoint pruning
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Preserves local-compression summary messages across native OpenAI Responses compaction's pre-checkpoint pruning (`agent/native_compaction.py`), so a compression handoff never silently vanishes from the model's view once a server-side checkpoint has been replayed. Fixes #90975. --- ## Technical details ### 1. Canonical summary detection, not a heuristic `_is_summary_item` delegates entirely to `agent.context_compressor.is_compaction_summary_message` — the same provenance check every other summary consumer (memory providers, frontends, the compactor itself) already uses. It prefers the exact `COMPRESSED_SUMMARY_METADATA_KEY` flag and falls back to the canonical prefix classifier (handles the merge-into-tail shape too) for the case where the underscore-prefixed key was stripped by a wire sanitizer. No ad-hoc key scanning, no matching on content headings like `"## Summary"` in ordinary text. ### 2. Whole-or-drop retention, never a byte slice Retained summaries carry structural framing (handoff prefix, end marker, merge-into-tail delimiters) that a blind character slice can corrupt. A summary that doesn't fit `RETAINED_SUMMARY_TOKEN_BUDGET` (32k tokens) is dropped whole instead of truncated. `RETAINED_USER_MESSAGE_TOKEN_BUDGET` (64k tokens, Codex CLI parity) keeps its existing head-truncation behavior for retained user messages only. ### 3. Idempotent across repeated checkpoints A summary already retained once (identical text) is never duplicated across repeated checkpoint sequences. ### 4. Source-based recovery for lossy carrier shapes A canonical summary can be merged into an existing tail message rather than inserted standalone (`ContextCompressor` merge-into-tail). By the time that message becomes a Responses input item, two real shapes lose or shadow the summary before pruning ever runs: - a **tool-result carrier** becomes a typed `function_call_output` — no `content`/`role` survives the conversion at all, and the pruner's type filter skips every non-`message` item; - an **assistant carrier** can be shadowed by a stale `codex_message_items` exact-replay captured *before* the merge rewrote its content — the replay path wins over the rewritten `content` for prefix-cache continuity. `_chat_messages_to_responses_input` now threads `item_sources` — the raw chat message each converted item came from — through to `prune_pre_checkpoint_items`. When a source is itself a canonical summary carrier, its content is read directly from the source (never from the lossy converted item) and retained as a synthesized `role="assistant"` message. This never orphans a `function_call_output`/`function_call` pair: the original typed item is fully replaced, not retained alongside a dropped partner. ### 5. `enable_summary_retention` Function-level override for tests and callers that need pre-#90975 behavior back. Not wired to a user-facing config surface — there is no `agent` reference at the actual call site (`codex_responses_adapter.py`) to wire real config without much broader plumbing. --- ## Test plan - [x] `tests/run_agent/test_native_compaction_summary_retention.py` — canonical detection, negative witnesses (a `"## Summary"` heading in ordinary text, a `False`-valued flag, an arbitrary underscore key never misclassify), whole-or-drop truncation, idempotency, live `ContextCompressor` marker emissions, and two new adapter-level witnesses feeding real merge-into-tail carrier shapes (tool-result, assistant-with-stale-`codex_message_items`) through the real `_chat_messages_to_responses_input(..., native_compaction_eligible=True)` with a replayed checkpoint. - [x] `tests/run_agent/test_native_compaction.py`, `tests/agent/test_compressed_summary_metadata.py`, `tests/agent/test_codex_responses_adapter.py`, `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent_codex_responses.py`, `tests/run_agent/test_provider_parity.py`, `tests/run_agent/test_codex_multimodal_tool_result.py` — no regressions (117 passed). - [x] `ruff check` clean on all changed files. --- ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'dark', 'themeVariables': { 'primaryColor': '#00f0ff', 'mainBkg': '#0a0a16', 'primaryTextColor': '#ffffff', 'primaryBorderColor': '#ff007f', 'lineColor': '#00f0ff'}}}%% graph TD A[Compressor Merge-Into-Tail] -->|Stamps COMPRESSED_SUMMARY_METADATA_KEY| B[Chat Message Source] B -->|role=tool| C[Lossy: function_call_output] B -->|role=assistant + stale codex_message_items| D[Lossy: Stale Exact Replay] B -->|item_sources mapping| E[Pruner Reads Source Directly] C -.->|old bug: type filter skips it| F[Summary Lost] D -.->|old bug: replay shadows rewrite| F E -->|Canonical Content, Whole-or-Drop| G[Synthesized Assistant Message] G --> H[Checkpoint Run + Retained + Post] H --> I[Wire: Summary Survives Exactly Once] ``` ## Infographic:

signal.title: Desktop app relaunch after in-app update fails to reconnect to WSL backend, requires manual close and reopen
signal.text: ## Symptom After clicking update from the About page on a Windows + WSL2 setup, the update runs and completes successfully (build stamp advances, exit code 0, source tree syncs to latest). The hand-off script relaunches the desktop app automatically. However, the relaunched app fails to reconnect to the WSL backend and stays in a failed state. The user must manually close the app and reopen it to get a working connection. This happens on every update attempt, not intermittently. ## Repro 1. Open the desktop app on Windows + WSL2 (desktop connects to `http://localhost:9119`) 2. Go to About page, observe updates available 3. Click update 4. The update overlay runs, the desktop closes, the hand-off script runs `hermes update` on the Windows side 5. The hand-off script completes with exit code 0 and relaunches the desktop (detached) 6. The relaunched desktop shows a boot failure: "Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket" 7. The app does not recover on its own. User must manually close it and reopen 8. After manual reopen, the app connects normally and the update is confirmed present ## What I expected After the hand-off script completes and relaunches the desktop, the app should reconnect to the WSL backend and present a working chat surface without manual intervention. ## What actually happens The relaunched desktop hits liveness probe failures and "Desktop boot failed: Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket" errors. From the user's perspective, the update failed and the app is broken. The only way to recover is to manually close and reopen. ## Evidence Desktop log showing the update trigger, relaunch, and boot failures: ``` [2026-08-20T18:07:13.253Z] [updates] restart: Updating Hermes — this window will close and the updater will open. [2026-08-20T18:07:14.388Z] [updates] launched repo hand-off script: windows.ps1 (branch main); exiting desktop to release venv shim [2026-08-20T18:13:03.270Z] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend [2026-08-20T18:13:03.667Z] [boot] Connecting to remote Hermes backend at http://localhost:9119 [2026-08-20T18:13:03.670Z] [boot] Remote Hermes backend is ready ``` Hand-off log showing successful update and relaunch: ``` 2026-08-20T13:13:02-05:00 update| ✓ Update complete! (v0.20.4) [main @ 59795c40f] 2026-08-20T13:13:02-05:00 hermes update exit code: 0 2026-08-20T13:13:02-05:00 removed update marker (owned) 2026-08-20T13:13:03-05:00 relaunching desktop: C:\Users\Krekos\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked\Hermes.exe 2026-08-20T13:13:03-05:00 desktop relaunched detached (pid 18420) 2026-08-20T13:13:03-05:00 focused relaunched desktop window ``` The update itself succeeds. The build stamp advances correctly. The problem is specifically the post-update relaunch failing to establish a stable backend connection from the user's perspective, even when the log shows a brief "ready" state. Liveness probe failures also appear during WSL backend restarts (not just post-update), suggesting the backend may not be fully ready to accept WebSocket connections when the desktop first tries to reconnect: ``` [hermes] Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe (1/3); keeping connection for retry. [hermes] Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe (2/3); keeping connection for retry. [hermes] Cached remote Hermes backend failed liveness probe; dropping stale connection. [hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket. Try reconnecting. ``` ## User impact Every in-app update requires manual intervention to recover. The user sees an error state after the update completes and has no way to know whether the update succeeded without manually closing, reopening, and checking the About page. This undermines confidence in the update flow that #88827 fixed. ## Environment - OS: Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu) - Backend: Hermes Agent v0.20.4, WSL `hermes serve` on port 9119 - Desktop: Hermes Electron app, package 0.17.0, built from `59795c40` - Desktop source: `C:\Users\Krekos\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent` - Backend source: `/home/krekos/.hermes/hermes-agent` - Connection: Desktop app connects to `http://localhost:9119` (remote mode, OAuth) ## Related issues - #88827 (closed) — Fixed the update flow to run the full multi-target update including desktop rebuild. This issue is the next step: the update runs correctly but the post-update relaunch fails to reconnect. - #88251 (closed) — Fixed the `get-windows` binding staging. Not related to this restart issue.

signal.title: Desktop sidebar should separate Projects and Sessions into independent sections with their own sorting menus
signal.text: ## Problem The desktop sidebar currently renders Projects and Sessions as the same section. A "grouping" setting (date, profile, project, status) changes what the section header says and what content appears underneath. You can either see your flat sessions list OR your project overview, but never both at the same time. Switching between them is buried in a filter menu dropdown that also contains nine other controls: ordering, status filter, project filter, profile filter, PR filter, archived toggle, card row toggle, row meta toggle, and the grouping mode itself. This makes the sidebar hard to navigate, especially once you start actively using projects. Sessions assigned to a project disappear from the flat list when you switch to project grouping, so you lose track of where things are. The mental model is "one section that transforms" instead of "two sections that coexist." ## What I'd like Separate Projects and Sessions into two independent sidebar sections, each with their own header, expand/collapse, and sorting menu. Similar to how Claude Desktop handles this. **Sessions section:** - Always visible, shows all chat sessions (API, Telegram, TUI, etc.) - Has its own sorting menu (date, status, pinned, etc.) - Sessions that are assigned to a project can either be duplicated here (like Claude Desktop) or filtered out when a "hide project sessions" toggle is on. Either approach works. The key is that this section exists independently and always has its own controls. - Pinning works within this section **Projects section:** - Separate row in the sidebar (alongside Pinned, Telegram, API, Cron Jobs, etc.) - Has its own sorting menu (alphabetical, recent activity, custom drag order) - Clicking a project expands it to show that project's sessions underneath - Sessions under a project can be pinned within the project - The project section's sorting and filtering do not affect the Sessions section and vice versa ## Why this is better than the current design The current design tries to do everything in one space with a grouping toggle. That means: - You can never see projects and sessions at the same time - Nine controls are crammed into one filter dropdown - Assigning a session to a project makes it harder to find in the flat list - The section header changes meaning depending on which mode you're in (which was the original confusion reported in #62537) Two separate sections with similar functionality and independent sorting would solve all of these. Projects become a first-class navigation surface instead of a view mode on the sessions list. ## Related issues - #62537 (open) — Reported the header mislabeling when the source filter toggle changes the section name. This is a symptom of the same root design: one section that transforms based on grouping mode. Separating Projects and Sessions would make #62537 moot. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop (Electron) on Windows 11 + WSL2 - Hermes v0.20.4, desktop package 0.17.0

signal.title: fix(mcp): restrict catalog environment writes
signal.text: ## Summary - restrict MCP catalog credential submissions to environment variables declared by the selected catalog entry - block Hermes runtime and approval-control variables at the shared environment writer - prevent generic persistence from replacing the MCP catalog trust root - apply denylist and `.env` key matching with native Windows case semantics while preserving POSIX behavior - validate the complete catalog environment map before writing any values - add endpoint-level regression coverage for valid credentials, undeclared keys, reserved controls, and secret-safe errors ## Security `POST /api/mcp/catalog/install` previously accepted an arbitrary `env` mapping and persisted each non-empty value to the selected profile's `.env` file before installation. A request could therefore attach a Hermes runtime control such as `HERMES_YOLO_MODE` to an otherwise valid MCP credential submission. The route now treats each catalog entry's `auth.env` list as a closed schema. Any undeclared name returns HTTP 400 before the first write or install action. The complete submitted name set is also checked against the shared writer denylist, so a malformed catalog entry cannot authorize itself to persist approval or session controls. Errors report rejected names only; submitted values are not included. ## Compatibility The Desktop already renders and submits credential fields from the selected catalog entry's `auth.env` declaration, so valid catalog installs retain their current request shape. Existing manually configured MCP servers are unchanged. The denylist remains name-specific rather than blocking all `HERMES_*` variables. Integration credentials and settings such as `HERMES_LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY`, `HERMES_SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`, `HERMES_QWEN_BASE_URL`, and `HERMES_MAX_ITERATIONS` remain writable. Dedicated CLI, config, and session controls continue to manage approval behavior. `HERMES_OPTIONAL_MCPS` is blocked only through generic persistence writes. Existing `.env` values and package-manager/process-supplied catalog roots continue to resolve. Windows comparisons are case-insensitive, matching the host environment model; POSIX comparisons remain case-sensitive. ## Test plan - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_config.py tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_catalog.py tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_catalog_env_boundary.py tests/hermes_cli/test_credential_lifecycle.py tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server_profile_unification.py -q` — 154 passed, 1 Windows-only integration skipped locally - [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_mcp_catalog_env_boundary.py -q` — 6 passed - [x] Ruff on all changed Python files - [x] `git diff --check` ## Verification note A broader `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/ -q` run reached unrelated update/doctor tests that detected the developer machine's live gateway and triggered the suite's live-system guard. The guard blocked attempts to signal those external gateway PIDs, producing 13 failures in update/doctor modules. None of the affected MCP/config/profile modules failed; those modules were rerun separately against the final diff as listed above.

signal.title: fix(file-tools): stale write_file overwrites are refused before disk mutation (#65604, salvage #65605)
signal.text: ## Summary `write_file` can no longer overwrite an existing file the task never read, or a file that changed on disk after the last read — the stale-write refusal now fires BEFORE disk mutation instead of warning after the data loss already happened. Salvage of #65605 by @danspicytaco (fixes #65604), cherry-picked with authorship preserved, plus hardening on top. Also scouted from MoonshotAI/kimi-code#3096 (their agent-core-v2 `staleGuard` feature, merged this week) — same design conclusion independently: veto Edit/Write pre-execution on never-read or mtime-changed targets, refresh the baseline after own writes so consecutive self-writes stay unblocked. ## Changes - `tools/file_tools.py` (contributor commits, cherry-picked): - New per-task `full_write_baselines` set: populated by full, non-partial, **unredacted** `read_file` and by successful `write_file`; `patch` intentionally does not qualify. - `write_file_tool` refuses (pre-mutation, `stale_write_blocked: true`) when the target exists but has no baseline, or when cross-agent/mtime staleness is detected; refusal message tells the model to re-read → merge → retry. - Redacted reads never bless a full overwrite (prevents persisting the `«redacted:…»` sentinel back into credential files — the #35519 corruption class). - `patch` remains warning-only; new-file creation unaffected; capped container (`_FULL_WRITE_BASELINES_CAP`) + `_new_read_tracker_task()` consolidation. - Hardening commit (ours): - Redacted-read test force-enables redaction (hermetic CI has no config), matching `tests/agent/test_redact.py` convention. - `test_write_verification` CRLF case establishes a read baseline first — sibling test pinning the old overwrite-without-read behavior, updated to the new contract. - `website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md` documents the read-before-overwrite contract. - `contributors/emails/` mapping for DanSpicyTaco. ## Validation | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | write_file on unread existing file | silently overwrites | refused pre-mutation, file untouched | | write after external on-disk edit | warning attached *after* clobber | refused pre-mutation, external edit preserved | | consecutive same-task writes | ok | ok (own write refreshes baseline) | | redacted read → full overwrite | could persist redaction sentinel | refused | | patch / new-file creation | ok | unchanged | Targeted suites: 139 passed, 2 skipped (`test_file_staleness`, `test_file_read_guards`, `test_file_tools`, `test_file_state_registry`, `test_cross_profile_guard`, `test_write_verification`, `test_line_ending_preservation`). E2E against real file I/O in an isolated `HERMES_HOME`: 7/7 scenarios (unread-refusal, read→write, consecutive write, external-edit refusal, re-read heal, new file, patch untouched). Closes #65605 (salvaged, authorship preserved). Fixes #65604. ## Infographic ![Stale Write Guard mission patch](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aa72bb1/YYEQRJSXewPNJ1NQzxs9C_gIFLMwZI.png)

signal.title: Gateway self-heal wedges after Telegram polling network outage — reconnect watcher never takes over
signal.text: # Gateway self-heal wedges after Telegram polling network outage (2026-08-20) **Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)** | Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0-28) | Python 3.12.3 Messaging: telegram (polling mode, direct connection, DoH-discovered fallback IP) + weixin Deployment: `systemd --user` service `hermes-gateway.service` (Restart=always) ## Summary After a Telegram long-polling network outage, the gateway's retryable-fatal error path **wedges the main loop**. The adapter correctly marks the platform retryable-fatal after 10 failed reconnect attempts, but the supervisor handler (`_handle_adapter_fatal_error`) logs the ERROR line and then **never proceeds** — the expected `queued for background reconnection` / `gateway staying alive, watcher will retry` log lines never appear, and the background reconnect watcher never takes over. Telegram stayed disconnected for **4h17m** until a manual process re-start. The cron scheduler (separate asyncio task) kept running normally the whole time; only the messaging main loop was wedged. ## Timeline (all times CST, UTC+8) | Time | Event | |---|---| | ~03:50 | Telegram long-poll connection reset (empty error, CLOSE-WAIT socket seen at 03:50:21) — typical network-path reset on direct connection | | 03:50:01 -> 04:02:31 | 10 exponential-backoff retries (5s->60s cap), all failed, error text empty | | 04:02:31,296 | adapter: `Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries.` (logs "Restarting gateway.") | | 04:02:31,302 | gateway.run: `Fatal telegram adapter error (telegram_network_error): ...` | | 04:02:31 -> 08:07 | **COMPLETE LOG SILENCE** in both `gateway.log` and journald — no housekeeping, no reconnect attempts, no watcher activity. Cron jobs (agent.log) ran every 2 min uninterrupted. | | 07:00:45 | a cron job's `send_message` to Telegram **succeeded** (only a MarkdownV2 parse warning) -> network was back by 07:00, but the polling connection was never re-established (send-only, no receive) | | 08:07 | manual `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway` -> Telegram connected in 2s, everything recovered | ## Evidence (key log lines) ``` 2026-08-20 03:50:01,269 WARNING ...: [Telegram] Telegram polling degraded (heartbeat probe); gateway stays alive and will retry. Error: 2026-08-20 03:50:21,272 WARNING ...: [Telegram] updater.stop() timed out during network-error reconnect (likely CLOSE-WAIT socket); forcing drain and restart without clean stop 2026-08-20 04:02:31,296 ERROR ...: [Telegram] Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries. Restarting gateway. Last error: 2026-08-20 04:02:31,302 ERROR gateway.run: Fatal telegram adapter error (telegram_network_error): Telegram polling could not reconnect after 10 network error retries. Restarting gateway. ``` After the last ERROR line: nothing for 4h17m. PID stayed constant (207480); process alive, event loop alive (cron ran), but the gateway main loop produced no logging and performed no recovery. ## Root-cause analysis Code path: `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:2360` (`_polling_network_error_count > MAX_NETWORK_RETRIES` -> `_set_fatal_error(..., retryable=True)` + `_notify_fatal_error()`) -> `gateway/run.py:4325` `_handle_adapter_fatal_error()`. Expected sequence in `_handle_adapter_fatal_error`: 1. log ERROR (happened) 2. `_update_platform_runtime_status(...)` (unknown — no subsequent logs) 3. `await self._safe_adapter_disconnect(...)` (bounded by `_adapter_disconnect_timeout_secs`, ~210s default) 4. queue platform into `_failed_platforms` + log `queued for background reconnection` 5. log `gateway staying alive, watcher will retry in background` Observed: only step 1 produced output. Steps 2-5's log lines are absent from both `gateway.log` and journald for 4h17m. The reconnect watcher therefore never ran. `_safe_adapter_disconnect` is timeout-bounded, so the wedge is likely either in `_update_platform_runtime_status` (status file write path) or in an await that swallows CancelledError despite the `_await_adapter_cleanup_with_timeout` mitigation (e.g. `adapter.disconnect()` never yielding past the watchdog's cancel, with `consume_detached_task_result` keeping no visible trace). Notably, `errors.log` shows `updater.stop() timed out` (CLOSE-WAIT) earlier in the same outage, suggesting the python-telegram-bot teardown path was already wedged before the fatal handler ran. ## Impact - Telegram channel down ~4h17m (03:50 -> 08:07), only recoverable by manual process re-start. - All other gateway functions (cron scheduler, weixin send path, agent runs) unaffected. - This is the second failure mode of the same outage: the "keep gateway alive, reconnect in background" design (introduced to avoid re-start loops) failed to actually reconnect. ## Suggested investigation 1. Reproduce: simulate 10 consecutive Telegram network errors with a wedged socket and observe whether `_handle_adapter_fatal_error` reaches step 4. 2. Audit awaits between the ERROR log and the `_failed_platforms` enqueue for unbounded or cancellation-swallowing paths (especially `adapter.disconnect()` and the runtime status write). 3. Consider adding a watchdog on the platform-state file (`gateway_state.json`): if `telegram.state` stays non-connected for N minutes, force a hard re-start. ## Local mitigation (user side) A cron watchdog (`~/.hermes/scripts/gateway_watchdog.py`, every 5 min) now re-starts the gateway if `gateway_state.json` shows fatal/retrying/disconnected, or if `connected` has not refreshed in 15 min — with a 10-min re-start cooldown to avoid re-start storms. --- Reported by kevonlee (xwfl15632) · Hermes Agent v0.19.0 · 2026-08-20

signal.title: fix(acp): complete session/prompt on terminal session/update (#90952)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #90952 — `delegate_task(background=true)` from a gateway session spawning a `copilot-acp` subagent (harness `opencode acp` v1.18.18) hangs: the child never receives a response to its `session/prompt` request, the batch stays `state=running` until the 20-minute timeout, and the parent only gets a streamed ack. ## Root Cause Investigation (acp sources + Hermes shim): `session/prompt` only returns after `runUntilIdle` receives a `session.status == idle` event, which requires the SDK global-event subscription to connect to the ephemeral local HTTP server. In the detached gateway async path (child runs on the module-level `DaemonThreadPoolExecutor` with a stripped/profile-home env), that subscription can wedge — `initialize` / `session/new` still answer (they don't depend on the event connection), but `session/prompt` never resolves. Hermes' `_request()` then waits its full 900s budget and raises `TimeoutError("Timed out waiting for Copilot ACP response to session/prompt")` — the exact text in the batch's error summary. ## Change `agent/copilot_acp_client.py`: - New `_is_terminal_session_update(msg)`: recognizes a `session/update` whose `sessionUpdate` is a TERMINAL turn state (`turn_complete` / `turn_finished` / `complete` / `finished` / `done`, case-insensitive). - `_request()` for `session/prompt`: when text/thought parts have accumulated AND a terminal `session/update` arrives, the turn is complete — return the accumulated parts instead of continuing to wait for the wedged id-matched JSON-RPC result. Plain `agent_message_chunk` / `agent_thought_chunk` updates still do NOT complete the request; the id-matched result remains authoritative when it does arrive. ## Verification - `test_run_prompt_completes_on_terminal_session_update_without_result`: fake Popen emits initialize → session/new → `agent_message_chunk` ("Hello from the worker") → `turn_complete`, and NEVER the id=3 prompt result. `_run_prompt` returns the accumulated text. **RED without the fix** (`TimeoutError`), GREEN with it. - `test_run_prompt_still_waits_for_result_when_no_terminal_update` (control): without a terminal update the request still waits for the id-matched result and times out — the fallback does not fire on plain chunks. - Focused suite: 5 passed (`tests/agent/test_copilot_acp_client.py`). Closes #90952
