signal.title: fix(desktop): bind backend teardown to retained process authority (#89614)
signal.text: ## Scope and disposition This PR is the **Desktop retained process-authority slice** for #89614 across Windows and POSIX. It removes bare-PID / reconstructed-PGID teardown authority, makes reaped and PID-only records non-actionable, contains the complete Desktop-owned execution scope, and requires a completed handoff before any deliberate descendant escape. It does **not** close the repository-wide destructive-process-control class. The governing invariant remains: > A PID is observation, not destructive authority. The object proved to be owned must be the same object mutated by teardown, within the same generation and execution scope. This PR therefore **Refs #89614** and implements the Desktop slice of #90144. ## Windows authority contract Each marked Windows Desktop backend launch carries a fresh immutable envelope: - `HERMES_DESKTOP_PROCESS_GENERATION` - `HERMES_DESKTOP_PARENT_PID` - `HERMES_DESKTOP_PARENT_STARTED_AT_MS` - `HERMES_DESKTOP_PROCESS_AUTHORITY=windows-job-v1` Before Hermes imports spawn-capable code, the scoped Desktop bootstrap: 1. creates an unnamed Windows Job Object; 2. enables `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`; 3. opens and verifies the Electron parent through a retained kernel handle and creation-time marker; 4. assigns the current backend process through `GetCurrentProcess()`; 5. retains the Job and parent handles for the generation; and 6. closes the Job when the retained parent exits, reaping the root and contained descendants. Malformed envelopes, recycled-parent identity, handle failures, and assignment failures abort the marked backend. There is no `taskkill`, PID reconstruction, or fail-open fallback. ## POSIX authority contract Before the real `hermes_cli` package imports, the scoped bootstrap forks a small retained supervisor. The backend child becomes the leader of a fresh session, and the Electron `ChildProcess` remains bound to the supervisor that owns that exact generation. Descendants default to `contained`: - nested Python launches inherit the descendant guard before application imports; - `start_new_session`, positive `process_group`, `posix_spawn(setpgroup=...)`, direct `setsid` / `setpgid` / `setpgrp`, and equivalent group escapes are folded back into the retained scope or rejected; - opaque `preexec_fn` code is rejected because containment cannot be proved; and - natural root exit and retained-owner teardown reap contained residue without rediscovering authority from a PID or PGID. A deliberate `transferred` or `foreign` child requires a one-shot `ProcessTransferGrant`. A caller-authored receipt string is never authority. The old owner releases the child only after a receiving supervisor proves, through a bounded child-side acknowledgement, the exact token, receiver, owner SID/PGID, and target SID/PGID after the target crosses `exec`. The existing `windows_detach_popen_kwargs()` boundary now performs that handoff automatically on POSIX, preserving existing gateway/update/adapter detach consumers and composing with caller-supplied environments. The receiving owner supervises arbitrary Python, Node, shell, and native targets; graceful and forced `Popen` controls route through that receiver, which reaps its exact target scope. Missing or malformed ACK, sender death, target exec failure, or timeout fails closed and reaps before returning. ## Electron lifecycle contract `backend-child.ts` signals only a retained, explicitly live `ChildProcess` object. - accepted signal submission is `StopRequested`, not fabricated `Exited`; - only an observed exit is `Exited`; - a missing child is `AlreadyExited`; - PID-only or incomplete records are `NoAuthority`; - `child.killed` is treated as signal submission, not exit observation, so force escalation remains actionable; and - hard authority failures raise typed `BackendStopError` outcomes instead of disappearing behind swallowed booleans. Observed lockers and persisted ownership records remain diagnostic state and never become kill targets merely because they contain a PID. ## Exact implementation Current head: [`234c8948a15e3335b5595a85cfd20b0a469faaca`](https://github.com/andrexibiza/hermes-agent/commit/234c8948a15e3335b5595a85cfd20b0a469faaca) The final repair is one atomic fast-forward commit over `89e22c88eab98d586a221b30f94050eeb0545e75`, changing exactly ten files: the Desktop lifecycle boundary and tests, the scoped bootstrap, a modular POSIX authority/guard/transfer implementation, its retained receiving owner, and real topology witnesses. ## Exact-tree local verification ```text PYTHONPATH=/mnt/data/pr90250-work pytest -q \ tests/hermes_cli/test_posix_process_authority.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_process_authority_bootstrap.py 14 passed in 8.72s PYTHONPATH=/mnt/data/pr90250-work pytest -q \ tests/hermes_cli/test_posix_process_authority.py 8 passed in 8.16s python -m py_compile <all modified/new Python authority modules and tests> PASS npx --no-install tsc --noEmit --target ES2022 --module NodeNext \ --moduleResolution NodeNext --strict --skipLibCheck \ node-globals.d.ts apps/desktop/electron/backend-child.ts PASS compiled backend-child lifecycle runtime assertions PASS Windows/process-authority footgun pattern scan PASS ``` Topology coverage now includes contained grandchildren, an unrelated control process, positive PGID escape attempts, a real child-side handoff with explicit-env preservation, receiver-routed force stop without residue, missing-target rejection, natural-exit cleanup, and generation-N versus generation-N+1 fencing. The scoped bootstrap witness proves the retained supervisor never imports the real Hermes package. Exact-head hosted CI, Nix, and Docker were started by the implementation push and remain the landing evidence. ## Remaining repository-wide class closure #89614 remains open until the broader repository class is closed, including: - moving Windows authority to the native suspended-spawn boundary so Job assignment precedes any application instruction; - routing every production owned-process mutator outside Desktop through retained authority or an explicitly distinct service/sandbox/remote/foreign-process policy; - rejecting new direct PID/PGID mutators outside named authority boundaries; - preserving reused-PID and reused-PGID decoys; - proving authority crash/restart semantics; and - validating the actual packaged Windows Desktop/updater artifact for lock detection, graceful stop, residue abort, successful retry, descendant cleanup, and no foreign-process mutation. ## Topology and provenance - Refs #89614. - Implements the Desktop slice of #90144. - Supersedes the containment-only shape of #89689 without discarding its provenance or its identification of the update-loop recycled-PID mechanism. - Preserves #89614 / `@gebilaowang404` as the concrete P1 incident owner and #90144 as the proof-scope / mutation-scope class owner.

signal.title: [Feature]: Named/resumable sessions for cron jobs
signal.text: ### Problem or Use Case Every cron job invocation creates a brand-new session (auto-named with timestamp + hash, e.g. 20260421_135634_d8fa8a14). For recurring jobs that run every N minutes, this generates massive session bloat: - A job running every 20 minutes creates 72 new sessions per day - A job running every hour creates 24 new sessions per day - Over a month, a single cron job accumulates ~2,160 sessions These sessions are meaningless monitoring/health-check sessions that carry no conversation history worth preserving. They pollute the session directory, consume disk space, and slow down session enumeration. Expected Behavior Cron jobs should support a session parameter that allows specifying a named session to reuse across invocations. For example: yaml job: name: "Gateway Health Monitor" session: "gateway_health_monitor" # Reuse this session each run schedule: "every 20m" With this, each run of the job appends to the same conversation thread instead of creating a new session. The session would still exist but remain lean — just a short log of each cron run rather than a full isolated conversation. Benefits 1. Massive session reduction — 72 sessions/day → 1 session forever 2. Cleaner session directory — monitoring jobs no longer pollute session lists 3. Persistent short-term context — if the health check needs to remember the last state (e.g., "gateway was down 3 minutes ago"), it can without creating new sessions 4. Easier debugging — all health check runs are in one place, easy to review timeline of issues Implementation Notes - The session name should be a simple string identifier (no special characters) - If the session doesn't exist on first run, create it - The session could have a special marker/type to indicate it's a cron-reused session (for session cleanup/rotation logic) - Optional: support a max_session_history to keep the reused session from growing unbounded ### Proposed Solution cron job yaml file has session parameter that will append log data upon cron execution. ### Alternatives Considered deleting prior sessions that match a string. ### Feature Type Gateway / messaging improvement ### Scope Small (single file, < 50 lines) ### Contribution - [ ] I'd like to implement this myself and submit a PR ### Debug Report (optional) ```shell ```

signal.title: fix(session_search): recall the current session own early context (#90939)
signal.text: ## Summary `session_search` could not recall the **current session's own early context** in long live sessions. For a session that had outgrown the live context window, discovery returned `count: 0, sessions_searched: 0` for terms that existed verbatim in the current session's message store (FTS index complete, all rows `active=1`), forcing the agent to fall back to raw SQL against `state.db`. This PR makes current-session hits that have fallen out of the live window discoverable again, while keeping the existing behavior for short sessions, compaction archives, rewind rows, and foreign-session lineage dedup untouched. ## Root Cause In `tools/session_search_tool.py`, `_discover` skips FTS hits whose `session_id` is the current session, on the assumption that "the current session IS the current context". The only escape hatch was `_is_compacted_message` — rows archived by in-place compaction (`active=0, compacted=1`): ```python if current_session_id and raw_sid == current_session_id: if not is_compacted_hit: continue ``` That assumption breaks in a long live session: early turns leave the live window **without any archival mark** (`active=1, compacted=0` — the prune path never flips the compaction flag, and no compaction archive is produced). The heuristic then classified every same-session hit as "in context" and filtered the whole session out of discovery — including content that is provably no longer in the live window. The issue documents this exactly: 353-message session, 23–24 FTS hits for "gamelandia", `session_search` → `count: 0, sessions_searched: 0`. There is no persisted "live-context floor": the live window is token-bounded and nothing in the DB records where it starts, so `active=1` alone cannot distinguish in-context from out-of-context content. ## Change - **`_LIVE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_MESSAGES = 200`** — a conservative message-count ceiling for the live context window of the current session (the window is token-bounded; this is a safe upper bound on how many of the newest rows can still be inside it). - **`_live_context_floor_id(db, session_id)`** — returns the id of the oldest row that can still be in the live window (the newest `_LIVE_CONTEXT_WINDOW_MESSAGES` active rows), or `None` when the session is short enough that everything could still be in context. Fail-safe: any error returns `None`, preserving the old skip behavior. - **`_is_below_live_context_floor(db, session_id, message_id)`** — predicate used by the scroll gate. - **`_discover`**: same-session hits now surface when they are provably below the live-context floor. Hits inside the newest window rows (or short sessions with no floor) are still skipped as in-context; compaction-archived rows and compression-ended sessions keep surfacing as before; all other same-lineage and foreign-session logic is unchanged. - **`_scroll`**: the current-lineage guard now accepts anchors below the live-context floor, so a scroll on a discovery result that just surfaced a current-session early hit is not rejected as "already in your active context". Trade-off direction: when in doubt, the tool now leans toward surfacing (a redundant in-context hit costs a few tokens) rather than hiding (which caused total recall blindness for the current session's own history). ## Verification - New regression tests in `tests/tools/test_session_search.py` (`TestCurrentSessionEarlyContext`): - early current-session hits surface after the session outgrows the window (the #90939 repro shape — needle only in the first messages, all rows `active=1, compacted=0`); - a foreign-session hit still surfaces **and** dedupes by lineage (two foreign hits → one result; `count == 2`, `sessions_searched == 2`); - hits inside the newest window rows stay filtered (the escape does not widen to the whole session); - scroll accepts a below-floor current-session anchor returned by discovery. - Verified the 3 core regression tests **fail without the fix** (exactly the issue's `count: 0` behavior) and pass with it. - `tests/tools/test_session_search.py`: **57 passed** (was 53); `tests/run_agent/test_token_persistence_non_cli.py`: 3 passed. Full suite not run, per focused-change policy. ## Related Fixes the distinct trigger reported in #90939 (long live session, no archival mark). Existing compaction (#38763), `/new`-reset (#85756), and delegation-exclusion semantics are preserved and covered by the pre-existing tests. Closes #90939
signal.author: webtecnica

signal.title: fix(desktop): surface actionable error when Nous Cloud agent returns 503 (#85335)
signal.text: ## Fix for #85335 ### Problem When Hermes Desktop connects to a Nous-managed cloud agent (e.g. `https://ares-3009.agents.nousresearch.com`) and that backend returns **HTTP 502/503/504**, the error surfaced as a generic "Hermes backend did not become ready" message with no guidance that the cloud server itself is down — and the app appeared stuck in a retry loop. The user cannot restart a Nous-managed cloud instance themselves and had no actionable recovery path. ### Fix (whole class, all failure boundaries) Classifies a Nous Cloud **502/503/504** server-side fault at **every** startup boundary, carries a structured signal to the renderer, and renders an actionable recovery screen. Not just the one site the report hit: - **`backend-health.ts`** — `isServerSideHttpError` (structured-first on `err.statusCode`, legacy `^NNN:` prefix as fallback, non-`Error` inputs rejected), `isNousCloudAgentUrl`, and a single `makeNousCloudBackendDownError` factory. Used in `waitForHermesReady` (readiness exhaustion). - **`main.ts`** — runs the Cloud classifier at the **OAuth WS-ticket mint boundary** (`mintGatewayWsTicket`) before the `gatewayTicketFailure` wrap, so a Cloud 503 from the ticket endpoint surfaces the actionable message instead of the generic reachability error. 401/403 still route to reauth. Also carries `isCloudBackendDown` / `statusCode` through `DesktopBootProgress` so the renderer can key on the structured result. - **`connection-config.ts`** — `gatewayTicketFailure` preserves the source error's integer `statusCode` (401/403 → reauth, unchanged). - **`global.d.ts`** — `DesktopBootProgress` gains `isCloudBackendDown?` / `statusCode?`. - **`boot-failure-overlay.tsx`** — the recovery screen now branches on `isCloudBackendDown`: cloud-specific title/description, local-only **Repair dropped**, and the actionable portal / Local-mode / Discord guidance. The electron factory's full message is still shown in the error box. - **i18n** — `cloudDownTitle/Description/Hint` keys (en + ar/ja/zh/zh-hant). The actionable message a user now sees: names the failing cloud host, reports the HTTP status, points to https://portal.nousresearch.com, offers switching to Local mode, and gives the Discord support link. ### Tests - `backend-health.test.ts` — 502/503/504 structured + legacy + non-Error rejection, cloud-wrap on readiness exhaustion, non-cloud 503 not wrapped, factory shape/cause/guards. - `connection-config.test.ts` — OAuth ticket-mint **503 → transport failure with `statusCode` preserved**; **401 → reauth (never Cloud-down)**; integer-only statusCode copy. - `boot-failure-overlay.test.tsx` — cloud-down recovery renders, Repair dropped, portal guidance shown (4/4 passing). - TypeScript: `tsc --noEmit` clean across the desktop project (0 errors). ### Verification - Renderer overlay suite: 4/4 passing. - Electron suites: present but the vitest runner hangs in this environment (documented limitation); verified via the same direct-execution path the author used. Fixes #85335 Related (same debugging session, separate class): #85333 (read_file dedup) via #85353.

signal.title: Desktop sessions miss configured MCP tools and uvx servers can fail under macOS GUI PATH
signal.text: ## Bug description Configured MCP servers can be discoverable from the Hermes CLI but still be missing from Hermes Desktop sessions. I hit this with a native MCP server configured like this: ```yaml mcp_servers: linkedin: command: uvx args: - linkedin-scraper-mcp ``` The server itself was installed and healthy. Running the Hermes MCP diagnostic from the Hermes venv connected and discovered tools: ```bash /Users/dpearson/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python3 /Users/dpearson/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes mcp test linkedin ``` Result: ```text ✓ Connected ✓ Tools discovered: 17 ``` But the active Hermes Desktop/API session did not expose any `mcp_linkedin_*` tools, so the agent had to fall back to a manual FastMCP client path. There appear to be two separate issues here: 1. Desktop/dashboard WebSocket sessions do not start MCP discovery, so agents created from that path can snapshot tools before configured MCP servers are registered. 2. On macOS, Desktop/launchd processes can inherit a minimal PATH like `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`. That PATH does not include `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, or `/usr/local/bin`, so an MCP server configured as `command: uvx` can fail from Desktop even though it works from an interactive terminal. ## Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS, install/configure an MCP server using `uvx`, for example: ```yaml mcp_servers: linkedin: command: uvx args: - linkedin-scraper-mcp ``` 2. Verify it works from the Hermes CLI: ```bash hermes mcp test linkedin ``` 3. Start Hermes Desktop from the macOS app/GUI path. 4. Open a new Desktop/API session and ask the agent to use the configured MCP server. 5. Inspect the available tool schema or try to call the expected `mcp_<server>_*` tools. ## Expected behavior MCP servers configured in `config.yaml` should be discovered and registered for Hermes Desktop/API sessions the same way they are for CLI/TUI sessions. For `uvx` MCP servers, Desktop should either resolve `uvx` reliably under the macOS GUI environment or surface a clear startup/config error that explains the PATH problem. ## Actual behavior The MCP server was configured and reachable through Hermes MCP diagnostics, but the Desktop/API agent session did not expose the MCP tools. In my case, the server was `linkedin-scraper-mcp`; the missing tools were the expected LinkedIn MCP tools such as `mcp_linkedin_*`. ## Local mitigation applied I mitigated this locally with a small code patch: - Moved the background MCP discovery state out of `tui_gateway/entry.py` and into `tui_gateway/server.py`, which is imported by both the stdio TUI path and the Desktop/dashboard WebSocket path. - Updated `tui_gateway/entry.py` to call the shared `server.start_mcp_discovery_background()`. - Updated `tui_gateway/ws.py` to call `server.start_mcp_discovery_background()` before the Desktop/WebSocket session reports readiness. - Updated `_make_agent()` in `tui_gateway/server.py` to briefly wait for MCP discovery before snapshotting the agent's tool list, with a bounded timeout so slow/dead MCP servers do not block startup indefinitely. - Extended `tools/mcp_tool.py::_resolve_stdio_command()` to resolve `uv` and `uvx` under GUI-style PATHs, using these fallback locations: - `~/.local/bin/{uv,uvx}` - `/opt/homebrew/bin/{uv,uvx}` - `/usr/local/bin/{uv,uvx}` I also added a regression test for the Desktop/WebSocket startup path and kept the existing MCP command resolver tests passing. Local verification after the mitigation: ```text uvx -> /Users/dpearson/.local/bin/uvx uv -> /Users/dpearson/.local/bin/uv npx -> /Users/dpearson/.hermes/node/bin/npx ``` Test results: ```text tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_issue_948.py: 5 passed tests/tui_gateway/test_mcp_discovery_startup.py + MCP resolver tests: 8 passed py_compile over modified files: exit 0 ``` ## Environment - OS: macOS 26.5.1 - Hermes Agent: v0.15.1 (2026.5.29) - Repo: NousResearch/hermes-agent - Commit tested locally: `b34ee8074` - Python: 3.11.15 ## Notes This is not specific to LinkedIn. LinkedIn was just the MCP server that made the bug visible. Any Desktop-launched MCP server using `uvx` can hit the PATH issue, and any configured MCP server can be missed if the Desktop/WebSocket path does not start MCP discovery before the agent snapshots tools.

signal.title: fix(agent): avoid false-positive tool failure on {"error": null} (#91166)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #91166. `_detect_tool_failure` string heuristic flagged any result containing the literal `"error"` in the first 500 characters. Tools like `web_extract` that serialize `{"error": null}` on success were incorrectly classified as failures, counting toward retry thresholds and triggering "stop retrying this failing tool" guidance. ## Root Cause The generic heuristic at the end of `_detect_tool_failure()`: ```python if '"error"' in lower or '"failed"' in lower or result.startswith("Error"): return True, " [error]" ``` This matches `"error": null` — a valid success response — because it only checks for the key name, not the value. ## Fix Add a null-value exclusion: `"error"` followed by `: null` (after whitespace collapse) is not a failure. The structured JSON check above already handles this correctly for parseable JSON; this fix closes the gap for the string heuristic fallback. ## Changes - `agent/display.py`: Add `"error":null` exclusion to the string heuristic in `_detect_tool_failure()` ## Testing - `python3 -m py_compile agent/display.py` — OK - Reproducer from issue now returns `(False, "")` instead of `(True, " [error]")`

signal.title: fix(steer): keep pre-API delivery within current turn
signal.text: ## Summary - Re-anchor the active user-message boundary after successful pre-API compression. - Deliver pending steers only through tool results after that current-turn boundary; otherwise preserve them for the next safe delivery point. - Emit INFO delivery evidence only after marker insertion, and report immediate busy acknowledgements as accepted with delivery pending. ## Problem A steer accepted while pre-API compression rebuilt the transcript could reach the next loop with a stale `current_turn_user_idx`. The drain then scanned the entire history, appended the marker to a historical tool result, cleared the pending buffer, and reported success. A later assistant response makes that marker historical under the steer contract, so the model must ignore it. ## Related work [PR #51312](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/51312) adds a system-note fallback when no tool message exists anywhere. It still scans the entire transcript before that fallback, so compacted histories that contain historical tool rows remain vulnerable. This patch fixes the turn boundary directly without adding another delivery channel. ## Validation - Canonical per-file runner: 373 tests passed across the steer, compression, gateway busy-input, API-run, onboarding, and core conversation-loop suites. - The historical-tool regression fails when the old global backward scan is restored, then passes with the current-turn bound. - The pre-API compression regression fails while the user-message index remains stale, then passes after re-anchoring. - Ruff and `git diff --check` pass on the complete patch. ## Risk The change preserves message-role alternation, prompt caching, the existing post-tool delivery path, and queue fallback behavior. It adds no provider, schema, migration, or configuration surface.

signal.title: fix(desktop): union-roster bot handles were absent from @ autocomplete and mentions didn't route (#89303)
signal.text: ## Summary - The composer `@` autocomplete offered **zero** bot rows (local and remote alike), and remote-bot `@name-device` mentions never routed — issue #89303. - Root cause: `useRoster` caches under the 3-element key `[...ROSTER_KEY, activeConnectionId]`, but both the `mention-completions` provider and the mention-routing middleware read `getQueryData(ROSTER_KEY)` with the bare 2-element key. An exact-match lookup against a 3-element cache key returns `undefined` forever, so the provider saw an empty roster and the middleware fell back to a local-only `profiles.list`. - Fix: new `cachedUnionRoster()` helper — exact read of the live connection's cache entry, prefix-scan fallback (`getQueriesData`) keeping the freshest snapshot; never throws, callers keep their existing cold-cache fallbacks. Wired into both call sites. ## Reproduction (before) Typing `@` in any composer lists project file references only — no `@hermes`, no local profile handles, no `@name-device` remote handles. Typing the full qualified remote handle matches nothing. Matches issue #89303 exactly (remote Bot rows instruct the user to `@name-device` the agent; the completion surface never offers it). ## Test plan - [x] Hardened `mention-completions.test.mjs`: the `getQueryData` mock now reproduces real QueryClient v5 exact-key semantics (a bare 2-element `ROSTER_KEY` lookup misses the 3-element cache useRoster writes). Rationale: the old key-agnostic mock is exactly why this regression was invisible to CI. - [x] Verified the tests fail against the old code (`git stash` → 2 failures) and pass after the fix (**9/9 pass**, including renamed-bots tests). - [x] Built the desktop app (`npm run build`) and confirmed the fix in the produced bundle. - [ ] Manual: `@` in composer now lists local + remote (`· <Connection>` suffix) bots; selecting a remote handle routes the turn and the reply comes from the remote agent. Fixes #89303

signal.title: feat(discord): add request-owned guild settings to discord_admin
signal.text: ## Summary Implements Discord Feature Package **A5** as a request-owned action on the existing `discord_admin` authority. Exact head: `d4364a5d960ae0057b078059cdb9ecb6e0101322` Current-main parent: `4a5b6dd4512a10c3c18da3e5b9e5c7fb681cbfbb` Current diff: seven files; no second public model tool. ## Root cause closed The prior branch had two contradictory shapes: 1. a safe, transport-free `PATCH /guilds/{guild_id}` request builder; and 2. a separate `discord_guild_settings` model tool that duplicated token, allowlist, transport, and error ownership. That second tool could not participate correctly in `discord.server_actions`: the canonical allowlist validates names against `discord_tool._ACTIONS`, where the parallel action did not exist. Explicit allowlists therefore made the action impossible to enable, while tests hid the defect by monkeypatching the loader. This head removes that parallel ownership model. Bounded feature modules now contribute action metadata to the canonical `discord` / `discord_admin` tools, while the existing owner retains credentials, config policy, REST transport, dynamic schema, and 403 enrichment. ## Runtime contract `edit_current_guild_settings(settings)` is exposed only through `discord_admin` and: - requires an active Discord request context; - requires an authenticated Discord requester; - derives the target guild exclusively from `HERMES_SESSION_SCOPE_ID`; - ignores any model-supplied `guild_id` for this action; - resolves the active-profile bot token through the canonical Discord owner; - honors the real `discord.server_actions` allowlist; - rejects non-object, unsupported, malformed, out-of-range, and empty PATCH bodies before transport; - preserves explicit `false`, `0`, and `null` values; - returns canonical `MANAGE_GUILD` guidance on Discord 403 responses. The scalar request builder remains transport-free and restricted to approved settings. ## Architectural seam - `tools/discord_api/action_registry.py` defines bounded action metadata and rejects duplicate ownership/schema ambiguity. - `tools/discord_action_extensions_tool.py` composes discovered actions into the existing public tools without growing `tools/discord_tool.py` or registering another model surface. - `tools/discord_api/guild_settings_action.py` owns only A5 request-context validation and payload composition; credentials and transport remain canonical. This seam is reusable by the remaining Discord admin packages instead of repeating the same ownership bug. ## Verification Local pre-publication receipts: ```text python -m py_compile <new implementation and test files> pytest -q tests/tools/test_discord_action_registry.py tests/tools/test_discord_guild_settings_consumer.py 19 passed in 0.06s ``` The original guild-settings builder suite is retained. Hosted acceptance is exact-head CI attached to `d4364a5d960ae0057b078059cdb9ecb6e0101322`; no earlier green run is inherited. Fixes #86431 Part of #79564

signal.title: [Bug] Desktop v0.20.4: registered remote Bot handle is absent from composer autocomplete
signal.text: ## Summary Hermes Desktop v0.20.4 can discover a profile on a registered remote gateway and render its source-qualified Bot Mode row, but the qualified remote handle is absent from the normal composer `@` autocomplete. The row itself instructs the user to stay in the current chat and invoke that handle, so the advertised invocation path cannot be completed. ## Environment - Windows 11 Hermes Desktop, packaged build - WSL2 Linux remote gateway on the same machine, reached over loopback HTTP - Desktop and remote Hermes Agent: v0.20.4, commit `8911e2e0ed` - Connection registry: local app-managed gateway remains primary; one token-authenticated remote gateway is added No credentials, session tokens, private paths, or real profile display names are included below. ## Steps to reproduce 1. In **Settings -> Gateways**, keep **This device** as Primary. 2. Add a token-authenticated **Remote gateway** with a synthetic label such as `Lab Agent`. 3. Open **BOTS**. 4. Confirm the remote default profile appears exactly once as a source-qualified row, e.g.: ```text Lab Agent @default-lab-agent ``` The local row also remains exactly once, e.g. `Hermes @default-this-device`. 5. Click the remote row. 6. Observe Bot Mode's instruction to stay in the current chat and invoke `@default-lab-agent`. 7. Open a clean local chat and type a true lone `@`. 8. Inspect the entire scrollable autocomplete list, including its final entries. 9. Type the full qualified handle as an additional check. ## Expected behavior The remote source-qualified handle appears in autocomplete and can be selected as a genuine structured mention. Selecting it routes the turn to the registered remote gateway/profile and returns the remote agent's reply in the current chat. This is also the behavior described by #88060: the composer completion set should use the union agent roster, including `@name-device` handles for duplicate profile names across registered connections. ## Actual behavior - Discovery and deduplication pass: the local and remote Bot rows each appear exactly once. - The complete autocomplete list contains project references and local profile handles only. - The qualified remote handle is absent. - Typing the full handle reports no matching result. - A plain prompt sent after clicking the remote row remains on the current local profile, as expected for an unmentioned message; the remote agent is never invoked. ## Why this is a bug rather than a feature request The installed Bot Mode code deliberately treats `remoteSource` rows as mention-only entry points and tells the user to use the qualified handle. The same handle is then unavailable from the completion surface intended to provide Bot Mode handles. ## Impact A registered remote gateway looks healthy and its agents appear in BOTS, but users cannot exercise the supported cross-gateway invocation flow. Roster visibility can therefore be mistaken for end-to-end connectivity. ## Acceptance criteria - A lone `@` offers every invokable source-qualified remote Bot handle from the union roster. - Selecting the row creates a structured mention carrying connection + profile provenance. - The turn is written to the remote source's session database and the visible reply comes from that remote agent. - Local and remote profiles with the same name remain deduplicated and source-qualified. - Behavior survives Desktop restart and connection-registry reload. - An unreachable remote source surfaces a clear error instead of silently falling back to the active local profile. ## Related - #88060 — composer `@` autocomplete should offer Bot Mode agents (closed/implemented for the general case) - #88680 — preserve connection x profile route identity end to end - #89206 — adjacent non-primary Bot Mode chat/navigation failures

signal.title: fix(desktop): route bot mentions by focused profile
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes the Bot Mode mention path when the chat on screen belongs to a different profile than the gateway socket. A user can open a secondary bot's canonical chat while the Desktop gateway remains homed on `default`. The mention autocomplete and submit middleware were both using `host.state.profile` to decide which bot was speaking, so they still treated the default profile as self. A renamed default profile such as `Lucy` was therefore filtered out of autocomplete and a manually typed `@lucy` did not route, even though the secondary bot was visibly focused. There was a second prerequisite bug: `useRoster()` writes under the connection-scoped key `[...ROSTER_KEY, connectionId]`, while both mention readers used the shorter exact key and missed the roster. This PR preserves ArthurFranckPat's #90936 commit verbatim with its original authorship, then adds the focused-session owner fix on top. The combined change is required for the reported path: correcting only the cache makes Bot rows available, but `host.state.profile` still filters the wrong bot. The generic backend profile rows explain the misleading partial behavior: renaming a secondary profile changes its canonical id, so `@renametest` appeared to work through `complete.path`; renaming `default` only changes `display_name`, leaving the backend fallback as `@default` / `@hermes`. ## Related Issue - Discord report: https://discord.com/channels/1053877538025386074/1540069696701730911 - Builds on merged rename support in #90592. - Consolidates the roster-cache correction from #90936 while preserving its contributor commit and authorship. - #89710 independently overlaps the same roster-cache seam but does not cover focused-session ownership. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js` - Read the connection-scoped union roster for autocomplete and submit middleware. - Resolve the speaking bot from `host.state.focusedSessionProfile` through the plugin's existing `$focusedBotProfile` compatibility ladder. - Use that same focused owner for autocomplete self-filtering, mention resolution, sender display name, and sender handle. - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-completions.test.mjs` - Model real QueryClient v5 exact-key behavior. - Regress gateway=`default`, focused=`renametest`, renamed default=`Lucy`: offer `@lucy` and exclude the actual focused bot. - `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/mention-handoff-quoting.test.mjs` - Regress the same split through submission: `@lucy` routes to canonical profile `default` with Renametest as the sender. ## How to Test 1. Run `node --test "src/plugins/hermes-bots/tests/*.test.mjs"` from `apps/desktop`. 2. Open Bot Mode with the gateway socket homed on `default`, rename default to `Lucy`, and open another profile's Bot Chat. 3. Type `@`: `@lucy` should appear as a Bot completion, the focused bot should not offer itself, and submitting `@lucy ...` should route to profile `default`. Validation performed: - Focused mention/rename tests: 15/15 passed. - Full bundled Bot Mode suite: 343/343 passed. - Mutation proof: removing only the focused-session production change made exactly the new autocomplete and handoff regressions fail; restoring it returned both to green. - `git diff --check`: passed. - ESLint was not available in the isolated worktree because Desktop dependencies were not installed there (`globals` missing). GitHub CI remains authoritative for lint/build/typecheck. - No Python tests were run because this is a Desktop JavaScript-only change. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, Node behavioral tests in an isolated clean worktree ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A: behavior repair only; inline ownership comment updated - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — renderer-only state/cache selection; no platform APIs - [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A ## Screenshots / Logs The Discord report includes the before-state screenshot: the visibly focused Renametest chat showed only generic `@default`, `@renametest`, and `@hermes` `agent profile` rows, with no `Bot · Lucy` completion.

signal.title: fix(auth): use rightmost X-Forwarded-For value to prevent IP spoofing (#90702)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #90702. `_client_ip()` took the **first** `X-Forwarded-For` value, which is the original client address and trivially spoofable. An attacker could vary the leftmost XFF value to bypass the per-IP pending-authorization cap (`_MAX_PENDING_PER_IP = 8`) and fill the global store (256 entries) with 256 requests using unique spoofed IPs, blocking legitimate sign-in for up to 10 minutes. ## Fix Use the **rightmost** `X-Forwarded-For` value instead. This is the address appended by the nearest upstream proxy and cannot be set by the client. When no proxy is present, the direct socket peer address (`request.client.host`) is used as before. This is the standard approach recommended by OWASP and used by most web frameworks (Django's `HttpRequest.META['REMOTE_ADDR']` with `X-Forwarded-For` rightmost, Express.js `req.ip` with `trust proxy`). ## Changes - `hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py`: `_client_ip()` — use `fwd.split(",")[-1]` instead of `fwd.split(",")[0]` ## Testing - `python3 -m py_compile hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/routes.py` — OK - Single IP header: `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4` → `1.2.3.4` (unchanged) - Multi-IP header: `X-Forwarded-For: spoofed, proxy1, proxy2` → `proxy2` (rightmost)

signal.title: fix(memory): handle empty-string new_text alias in single-op path (#90468)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #90468. The single-op `new_text` alias fallback in `memory_tool()` only triggers when `content is None`, but some runtimes materialize omitted optional fields as empty string `""` rather than `None`/absent. This causes the alias to be skipped and returns a validation error. The multi-op path already handles this correctly using the `or` operator (`content = (op.get("content") or op.get("new_text") or "").strip()`). ## Changes - `tools/memory_tool.py`: Change `if content is None and new_text is not None:` to `if not content and new_text is not None:` to match multi-op behavior. ## Testing Verified the single-op path now correctly falls back to `new_text` when `content` is empty string.

signal.title: fix(api): require API_SERVER_KEY auth on GET /health (#90315)
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #90315. The `GET /health` endpoint on the API server returned HTTP 200 without checking `API_SERVER_KEY`, contradicting the documented requirement that all API server routes require authentication. This made it easy to mistake an authenticated server as open. The `GET /health/detailed` endpoint already has `_check_auth()` — this PR applies the same check to the simple `/health` endpoint. ## Changes - `gateway/platforms/api_server.py`: Add `_check_auth(request)` call to `_handle_health()` handler. ## Testing With `API_SERVER_KEY` set, `GET /health` without auth now returns 401 (matching `/health/detailed` behavior).

signal.title: fix(tools): resolve uv/uvx MCP commands under GUI-style PATHs (fixes #37589)
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes bare ``command: uv`` / ``command: uvx`` MCP server configs from Hermes Desktop on macOS. The Hermes Desktop app inherits a minimal LaunchAgent PATH (``/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin``) that doesn't include ``~/.local/bin`` (the uv user installer target), ``/opt/homebrew/bin`` (Apple Silicon Homebrew), or ``/usr/local/bin`` (Intel Homebrew / Linux from-source). A bare ``uvx`` MCP server therefore fails with ENOENT at ``execvp`` from Desktop even though it works fine from an interactive terminal — exactly the failure mode reported in #37589. ## Changes - ``tools/mcp_tool.py`` (``_resolve_stdio_command``) - Added ``uv`` and ``uvx`` to the bare-command candidate allowlist (was only ``npx``/``npm``/``node`` before). - Added ``$HERMES_HOME/bin/<cmd>`` as a candidate for managed uv/uvx (from #37660). Managed uv is preferred over ``~/.local/bin``, Homebrew, etc. so MCP servers use the same uv as the CLI update path. - Added a new ``/opt/homebrew/bin/<cmd>`` candidate for the Apple Silicon Homebrew case (``brew install uv``). The existing ``/usr/local/bin`` candidate continues to cover Intel Homebrew and Linux from-source builds. - Candidate ordering: Hermes-bundled Node → **managed uv** (``$HERMES_HOME/bin``) → ``~/.local/bin`` → ``/opt/homebrew/bin`` → ``/usr/local/bin``. - ``tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_issue_948.py`` - New test: ``test_resolve_stdio_command_finds_uvx_in_user_local_bin`` — covers the dominant install location for uv on Apple Silicon / Ubuntu. - New test: ``test_resolve_stdio_command_uvx_unchanged_when_already_on_path`` — ensures ``shutil.which`` still takes precedence (no double-resolve of a working bare command). - New test: ``test_resolve_stdio_command_skips_unknown_commands`` — negative test that catches the inverse regression of someone widening the allowlist so far that a bare ``command: my-tool`` gets rewritten to a coincidentally-named file at ``/opt/homebrew/bin/my-tool``. - New test: ``test_resolve_stdio_command_prefers_managed_uv`` — verifies that ``$HERMES_HOME/bin/uv`` wins over a stale ``~/.local/bin/uv`` (cross-reference with #37660). - The 4 existing ``npx`` tests continue to pass unchanged. ## How to test 1. ``~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_mcp_tool_issue_948.py -q --timeout=60`` — 9/9 pass. 2. ``~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/ -q --timeout=60 -k "mcp"`` — no regressions in the broader MCP test surface. ## Notes - The CLI / TUI paths were never affected (they inherit a full terminal PATH). This is a Desktop/launchd-only fix. - Sandbox / docker config can still pass an explicit ``env.PATH`` and the resolver will still honour it via ``_prepend_path``. The fallback is only consulted when the bare command isn't on the inherited PATH at all. - No change to behaviour for any command outside the ``npx/npm/node/uv/uvx`` allowlist — random bare commands like ``python`` or ``my-tool`` are left alone (the new negative test pins this). - The managed-uv candidate (``$HERMES_HOME/bin``) was added in coordination with #37660, which introduced managed uv at that location. Without it, MCP servers on Desktop would fall back to a stale ``~/.local/bin`` or brew-managed uv instead of the hermes-managed one. Closes #37589

signal.title: fix(desktop): make explicit connection identity authoritative
signal.text: ## Summary Follow-up to merged #89719. The registry bridge was still inferring identity from endpoint shape even when a descriptor was already registry-qualified, and legacy inference selected the first endpoint match. This closes that residual contract: - an explicitly present `connectionId` is authoritative only when it exactly names a registered connection; - explicit blank, null, undefined, or unknown IDs fail closed and never fall back to endpoint inference; - only descriptors with no `connectionId` property use the v1 compatibility bridge; - legacy local, SSH, and URL inference succeeds only for exactly one match; zero or multiple matches fail closed. ## Proof Adds focused witnesses for: - authoritative ID despite contradictory endpoint fields; - invalid explicit qualification with a misleading inferable endpoint; - unique legacy local/SSH/URL compatibility; - ambiguous URL, SSH, and local matches. Built directly on current `main` parent `f43eabee5f36e11448086ee8ee17c499958e81bf`; the commit diff is limited to the helper and a focused test file. ## Topology / provenance Follow-up to #89719 and #88325. This does not replace the original multi-connection work or its authorship; it closes the post-merge identity-authority residual.

signal.title: fix(gateway): do not auto-TTS A2A replies
signal.text: ## Summary Desktop **Read replies aloud** persists `voice.auto_tts` as a *global* gateway default. The runner then treats that default as “speak every reply on every platform that has no `/voice` mode.” A2A inbound is `MessageType.TEXT`. The A2A adapter has no native `send_voice`. Result: a completed text reply is synthesized to `tts_reply_*.mp3`, then: ``` [A2A] send_voice fallback: native audio send unavailable ⚠️ Couldn't deliver the audio attachment. ``` The peer sees a failed audio attachment instead of the text. Observed on v0.20.4 after an update flipped `auto_tts` true; earlier A2A text deliveries on the same hosts were clean. ## Change - `_should_send_voice_reply` returns `False` for platform `a2a`. - `_sync_voice_mode_state_to_adapter` never copies the global default onto the A2A adapter. - Regression: A2A + `adapter_auto_tts=True` stays text; Telegram with the same default still voices. `/voice on` / `/voice tts` on Discord/Telegram are unchanged. ## Test plan - [x] Isolated smoke: before patch, A2A text + global auto-TTS → `_should_send_voice_reply` **True**; after → **False**; Telegram still **True**. - [x] `test_should_send_voice_reply_a2a_ignores_global_auto_tts` passes. - [ ] CI gateway voice tests. signal.title: build(photon): upgrade spectrum-ts to 12.8.0
signal.text: ## Summary - upgrade the Photon sidecar from exact `spectrum-ts@8.0.0` to exact `12.8.0` - raise the sidecar Node engine to the repository floor (`>=22.22.0`) - declare `ffmpeg-static` so Spectrum can convert MP3 TTS output into native AAC/M4A voice notes - remove the obsolete Spectrum 8 compiled-code mixed-attachment patch from npm install, Node startup, Python startup, writable-sidecar mirroring, Docker builds, tests, and docs - retain and validate the OTel/protobuf security overrides against the Spectrum 12 tree - add a dependency/migration contract covering exact versions, engine floor, lockfile resolution, Docker references, patch removal, FFmpeg, and security overrides Companion to #91129, which keeps opaque inbound CAF recognition independently reviewable. ## Why Hermes upstream currently pins Spectrum 8. Controlled live testing against the same Photon project, validated secret, registered E.164 user, existing chat GUID, and audio fixtures showed: | Stack/path | Result | |---|---| | Hermes-pinned Spectrum 8 text | succeeds | | Spectrum 8 M4A `attachment()` | `target_not_allowed` | | Spectrum 8 M4A `voice()` | `target_not_allowed` | | Spectrum 12 M4A `attachment()` | succeeds and plays on-device | | Spectrum 12 M4A `voice()` | succeeds as a native voice bubble | | Spectrum 12 raw MP3 `attachment()` | succeeds unchanged | | Spectrum 12 raw MP3 `voice()` without FFmpeg | expected `ffmpeg unavailable` failure | | Migrated Hermes sidecar raw MP3 `voice()` with bundled FFmpeg | succeeds as a native voice bubble | This proves the pinned Spectrum 8 stack fails these media sends while the current Spectrum 12 stack succeeds. It does **not** claim that any single transport implementation detail is the isolated cause; multiple SDK generations changed together. ## Obsolete patch removal Spectrum 12's iMessage mapper natively preserves ordered text and attachment parts. The old `patch-spectrum-mixed-attachments.mjs` targets Spectrum 8 compiled output and cannot apply to v12. Leaving any of its install/runtime references would break fresh installs or sidecar startup. Removal covers: - sidecar `postinstall` - `index.mjs` import/execution - Python `_start_sidecar()` execution - writable mirror file list - Docker `COPY` - patch-specific tests - upgrade documentation ## Test-driven verification The migration contract was written first and failed on Spectrum 8: ```text 3 failed: old Spectrum pin, old postinstall patch, old lockfile ``` After implementation: ```text pytest tests/plugins/platforms/photon/ -q 130 passed npm ci passed npm audit 0 vulnerabilities node --check index.mjs passed git diff --check passed ``` The migrated sidecar's real loopback `/send-attachment` endpoint was then exercised against a live shared-line Photon project while the production gateway was stopped: ```text healthz HTTP 200 M4A attachment HTTP 200 + message ID M4A native voice HTTP 200 + message ID raw MP3 attachment HTTP 200 + message ID raw MP3 native voice + FFmpeg HTTP 200 + message ID sidecar shutdown exit 0 ``` On-device screenshots confirmed distinct ordinary audio attachments and native waveform voice bubbles, including the MP3 converted by bundled FFmpeg. The launchd-supervised Hermes gateway was restored afterward and Photon reconnected with no new credential errors. ## Independent review - Grok 4.6 reasoning review: supported the v8-fails/v12-succeeds conclusion, rejected overclaiming HTTP as the sole cause, recommended a companion PR, and identified the v8 patch as obsolete. - Antigravity `agy` / Gemini 3.1 Pro High pre-migration review: identified patch/engine/lockfile migration points. - Antigravity finished-diff review: **APPROVE WITH EVIDENCE**, no P0-P2 findings. During review, deleting all npm overrides was tested and rejected: a clean v12 tree produced 18 moderate OTel findings. Retaining the remediating overrides produced `npm audit: 0 vulnerabilities` and passed all automated and live acceptance checks. ## Residual risks - OTel overrides are security-motivated and tested, but subtle telemetry formatting/export differences remain possible. Photon telemetry is disabled by default in this integration. - `ffmpeg-static` downloads its platform binary during npm install. Air-gapped or egress-restricted builds may need `FFMPEG_BINARIES_URL`, a proxy, or a pre-baked dependency layer. - The live acceptance matrix covered a shared-line DM. Group behavior remains covered by existing automated tests and should remain part of release smoke testing. ## Rollback No database or credential schema changes. Revert this commit and run the sidecar's normal `npm ci`/setup path to restore the exact Spectrum 8 lockfile. The deleted compatibility patch returns with the revert.

signal.title: fix(desktop): preserve authoritative connectionId, fail-closed legacy fallbacks — #90048
signal.text: ## Summary Preserve the exact registered-gateway identity established before dialing and close the shipped residual from #89719. `resolvedConnectionId()` was a compatibility bridge, but the merged `hermes:connection` path could call it after dialing even when the descriptor already carried the exact `connectionId`. The helper ignored that proof and rebuilt a weaker identity from normalized URL or `user@host`, allowing first-match aliasing across distinct authorization and transport envelopes. This repair keeps #89719's gateway-switching architecture intact and reuses #88922's pre-dial identity contract as the single matcher. Closes #90048. ## Contract - A non-empty descriptor `connectionId` is authoritative. - Post-dial inference never overwrites it. - Descriptors without `connectionId` use compatibility inference only. - URL/Cloud fallback matches kind, URL, auth mode, token envelope, canonical headers, and Cloud organization. - SSH fallback matches host, user, defaulted port, key path, remote Hermes path, and remote profile. - Zero or multiple coarse candidates fail closed. - Zero or multiple exact-envelope matches fail closed. - Identity proof and current registry liveness remain separate concerns. ## Implementation - Extract the matcher introduced by #88922 into `connection-route-identity.ts`. - Import the same matcher from both `desktop-remote-route.ts` and `connection-registry.ts`. - Return an explicit descriptor ID before consulting the registry. - Gate genuinely weak legacy URL/SSH descriptors by candidate uniqueness before applying the exact shared matcher. - Remove the duplicate private matcher from `desktop-remote-route.ts`. ## Tests The regression matrix covers: - explicit-ID preservation under conflicting post-dial URL/auth/header metadata; - explicit retired IDs; - duplicate normalized URLs separated by auth mode, token envelope, headers, remote/Cloud kind, and Cloud organization; - exact duplicate URL envelopes; - same-host SSH entries separated by port, key path, remote Hermes path, and remote profile; - exact duplicate SSH envelopes; - fail-closed weak URL, Cloud, and `user@host` descriptors; - retained single-source migration compatibility. ## Verification - `git diff --check` - structural apply/reverse-apply validation against current-main changed regions - extracted matcher equivalence check against #88922's shipped implementation - strict focused TypeScript compilation: - `tsc --module commonjs --moduleResolution node --target ES2022 --strict --skipLibCheck` - executable focused identity harness: - `PR #90048 exact route identity harness: all assertions passed` Full repository Vitest and GitHub Actions should run on the opened exact-head branch. ## Artifact receipts Patch: `pr90048-exact-route-identity-v2.patch` SHA-256: `a145f30201468b34a1e7e1e924208b72ca4a04ebbf30db0b8bd2053d5b1ab68d` Lines: 702 Diff: 4 files changed, 474 insertions, 132 deletions Changed paths: - `apps/desktop/electron/connection-route-identity.ts` — new shared matcher seam - `apps/desktop/electron/desktop-remote-route.ts` — consumes the shared matcher - `apps/desktop/electron/connection-registry.ts` — authoritative-ID and fail-closed legacy fallback - `apps/desktop/electron/connection-registry.test.ts` — regression matrix Branch: `fix/89719-authoritative-connection-id` / commit `914d35d8` (from fork-push)

signal.title: [Bug]: @ context reference expansion aborts whole asyncio.gather and leaks sibling coroutines (missing return_exceptions=True)
signal.text: ### Bug Description `preprocess_context_references_async` in `agent/context_references.py` expands all `@` context references concurrently with a **bare** `asyncio.gather(...)` that has **no `return_exceptions=True`**. When a single reference expansion raises, the whole gather aborts, the exception propagates into the caller, and the still-running sibling coroutines are **left unawaited** (coroutine leak) — a classic asyncio hazard. This contradicts every other `gather` in the codebase, which uses the defensive `return_exceptions=True` pattern. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Send a message containing multiple `@` context references (e.g. `@file` + `@url`), where one of the references fails to expand (e.g. `url_fetcher` raises on that ref, or the file read errors). 2. Observe the exception from the failing ref propagate and abort the entire gather. 3. The concurrent sibling `_expand_reference` coroutines for the other refs are never awaited → coroutine leak ("coroutine was never awaited" / untracked tasks). ### Expected Behavior A failure in one reference expansion should be surfaced as a **warning** for that ref only, while the other refs' expansions complete normally. No coroutines should leak, and the caller should not crash. ### Actual Behavior A single ref failure aborts the whole gather, crashes/errors the caller, and leaks the sibling coroutines that were still running. ### Suggested Fix (mirrors existing pattern in codebase) ```python expanded = await asyncio.gather( *(_expand_reference(ref, cwd_path, url_fetcher=url_fetcher, allowed_root=allowed_root_path) for ref in refs), return_exceptions=True, ) for i, result in enumerate(expanded): if isinstance(result, BaseException): warnings.append(f"@ {refs[i].kind} reference expansion failed: {result}") continue warning, block = result ... ``` Affected location: `agent/context_references.py`, `preprocess_context_references_async` (gather begins at line ~267, unpack loop at ~278 on latest `origin/main`).

signal.title: feat(desktop): carry route activation proof into file mutations
signal.text: ## Summary - adds a typed `RouteActivationReceipt` that carries exact owner, activation generation, gateway realization, descriptor provenance, epistemic status, and readiness across Desktop activation - revalidates that receipt immediately before atomic profile/descriptor publication, so late generation N cannot publish after N+1 and same-named profiles on different sources cannot satisfy the no-op gate - routes read-only Desktop FS/Git facade calls through the gateway-owned connection context and requires a current exact receipt at the remote file-write boundary - keeps legacy/inferred routes usable for display/read-only paths while rejecting them as mutation authority ## Root cause The gateway registry already maintains an activation epoch and qualified `(connectionId, profile)` route, but `profile.ts` projected activation to `void | boolean` plus a separately resolved descriptor. Downstream code reconstructed authority from a bare profile, `$connection`, or endpoint-shaped state. `desktop-fs.ts` then dropped `connectionId` entirely before the side effect. That allowed: - late/superseded activations to publish renderer state; - same-profile routes on different sources to appear equivalent; - legacy inferred source identity to become apparent mutation authority; - remote FS writes to fall through a profile-only bridge request. ## Guarantees - activation completion is generation-monotonic; N cannot overwrite N+1 - an operation that never acquired a new activation generation cannot claim an existing route - profile publication consumes the activation receipt and revalidates generation, gateway object, and physical route in the same JS turn as the Nanostores batch - mutation authority additionally requires an authoritative exact descriptor proof and an open current gateway - presentation-only descriptor clones and reconnect-equivalent exact descriptors retain authority; owner/profile changes, inferred descriptors, and unqualified descriptors fail closed - exact registry writes carry `connectionId + profile` to the bridge - legacy inferred/unqualified remote routes remain degraded/read-only rather than silently acquiring current/default authority - local IPC writes and the existing fail-open display/navigation behavior are preserved ## Tests - exact local and registry-agent activation - stale generation and late completion - no-generation activation failure - source/profile mismatch - descriptor owner/profile mismatch - descriptor unavailability and legacy inference - shared-primary degradation - gateway realization replacement - descriptor clone retention vs route-changing replacement - exact remote file-write routing and mutation rejection - source-qualified FS cache identity - profile/agent publication and activation mutex regressions Local validation: - strict targeted TypeScript typecheck - 10-scenario runtime contention/authority harness - `git diff --check` ## Scope This is the first complete Desktop source → observable publication → mutation-boundary proof path for #90866. It does not close the repository-wide architecture umbrella; updater, persistence, transport, and packaged-realization paths remain separate migrations. Refs #90866 Refs #89916 Refs #90048

signal.title: fix(desktop): pin active-profile.json when creating a new profile
signal.text: ## Problem When a profile is created via the CLI (e.g. `hermes profile create mr_john --clone`), the desktop app's `active-profile.json` is never written. The file is only created when the user picks a profile in the desktop UI picker — CLI spawns bypass the UI entirely. Missing file → `primaryProfileKey()` falls back to `default` → the desktop silently launches the `default` backend instead of the new profile's backend. The new profile's tools and config are unreachable from the desktop surface — no error, no warning, just a quiet fail-open to `default`. This is a real footgun: a perfectly healthy CLI-spawned profile looks broken in the desktop because the backend is pinned to the wrong profile. ## Fix Call `_pin_active_profile()` at the very end of `create_profile()` — writes `{"profile": <name>}` to the desktop's `active-profile.json` (e.g. `%APPDATA%\Hermes\active-profile.json` on Windows). Uses the existing `desktop_userdata_dir()` helper from `gui_uninstall.py`, so the path resolution is already platform-correct. Best-effort and fully non-failing: if the desktop directory doesn't exist (headless installs) or is unwritable, the write is skipped silently. Profile creation always succeeds. ## Files - `hermes_cli/profiles.py` — new `_pin_active_profile()` helper (18 lines) + call site at the end of `create_profile()`. 24 insertions, 0 deletions. ## Testing - [x] `create_profile()` writes `active-profile.json` to the desktop userData dir - [x] Headless installs (no desktop dir) — no failure, profile created normally - [ ] Manual: CLI profile create → desktop relaunch → session lands on new profile with its tools visible

signal.title: fix(agent): contain an escaping ref failure in the concurrent @-expansion gather
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds the missing `return_exceptions=True` to the concurrent @-reference expansion gather in `preprocess_context_references_async`, so an exception escaping one `_expand_reference` call no longer aborts the whole batch. Under the bare gather, one escape propagated into the caller (failing the entire message over a single bad reference) and left the still-running sibling coroutines unawaited — a coroutine leak (#91221). This also matches the defensive gather pattern used everywhere else in the codebase. The escaped exception is contained as a per-ref warning (`@<kind>: expansion failed (...)`) while sibling references complete normally. `Exception` only is swallowed at the gather layer — `CancelledError`/`KeyboardInterrupt` are re-raised as results of `isinstance(..., Exception)` not matching them, so cancellation semantics are preserved. Note `_expand_reference`'s own except-block already converts ordinary per-ref failures (raising url fetcher, unreadable file) to warnings; the gather layer is the belt-and-suspenders for anything that escapes it, and it is what removes the abort-plus-leak behavior. ## Related Issue Fixes #91221 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `agent/context_references.py` — the gather gains `return_exceptions=True`; the reassembly loop zips refs with outcomes, converts an `Exception` outcome into a `@<kind>: expansion failed` warning and skips it, and re-raises nothing; rationale documented inline (#91221) - `tests/agent/test_context_refs_failure_isolation.py` — three regressions: a failing url fetcher surfaces a per-ref warning while both sibling refs land; an exception forced to escape `_expand_reference` entirely is contained (sibling awaited and landed, warning emitted, no exception reaches the caller); all-refs-failing still returns a result with one warning per ref ## How to Test 1. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/agent/test_context_refs_failure_isolation.py tests/agent/test_context_refs_concurrent.py -q` — should pass (5 passed) 2. Observed result: on unmodified main (verified via `git stash` control), `test_escaping_exception_is_contained_by_gather` fails — the escaped RuntimeError propagates out of `preprocess_context_references_async` and the sibling coroutine is never awaited (the #91221 abort-plus-leak shape); with this fix both coroutines complete and the failure is a warning 3. Regression: `tests/agent/test_context_refs_concurrent.py` (barrier-proven concurrency + output-contract ordering) and `tests/agent/test_plugin_context_references.py` (14 passed) — unchanged ## Checklist - [x] Code follows the project's style guidelines - [x] Self-review completed - [x] Comments added for complex logic (why return_exceptions, why Exception-only containment keeps cancellation propagating) - [x] Tests added that prove the fix (inner-failure isolation + escaped-exception containment + all-fail shape) - [x] All new and existing tests pass locally (5 + 14 passed; main-control fail confirmed) - [x] Platform: macOS (pure asyncio logic, platform-independent)

signal.title: [Bug]: gateway nested-PYTHONPATH duplication — inherited value appended as one string defeats dict.fromkeys dedupe (doubles every restart)
signal.text: ### Bug Description In `gateway/run.py`, `_ensure_windows_gateway_venv_imports()` (and the equivalent watcher branch in `GatewayRunner`) builds the new `PYTHONPATH` by **appending the inherited PYTHONPATH as a single string element** before `dict.fromkeys()` dedupes: ```python pythonpath = [project_entry, site_entry] if os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH"): pythonpath.append(os.environ["PYTHONPATH"]) # "a;b;c" appended as ONE element os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(dict.fromkeys(pythonpath)) ``` Because the inherited PYTHONPATH is appended as one raw string, `dict.fromkeys()` treats `"a;b;c"` as a single element and cannot dedupe its interior segments against `project_entry`/`site_entry`. Every gateway start that inherits a multi-segment PYTHONPATH **doubles** it: observed `2 -> 4 -> 8` segments. The bloated value is then inherited by every child process. Related but distinct from #57467 (which is about leaking PYTHONPATH *into other processes*): this is the gateway's own *duplication* of PYTHONPATH on every start. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. On Windows, start with an inherited `PYTHONPATH` containing multiple path segments (set by any launcher/venv activation — e.g. `C:\...\hermes-agent;C:\...\venv\Lib\site-packages`). 2. Start the gateway (`python -m gateway.run`). 3. Check `PYTHONPATH` in `_ensure_windows_gateway_venv_imports` after the build — the project/site entries now appear both as individual segments *and* inside the appended raw string. 4. Repeat a gateway restart — each start appends the (now duplicate-laden) inherited value again → segments accumulate / double with each restart. ### Expected Behavior `dict.fromkeys()` should actually dedupe — i.e. each PYTHONPATH *segment* should be matched individually, so repeated gateway starts keep PYTHONPATH stable instead of growing it. ### Actual Behavior PYTHONPATH doubles (`2 -> 4 -> 8`) on repeated gateway starts because the inherited value is appended as one raw string that `dict.fromkeys()` can't dedupe segment-wise. ### Suggested Fix (split before deduping) ```python if os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH"): pythonpath.extend(e for e in os.environ["PYTHONPATH"].split(os.pathsep) if e) os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(dict.fromkeys(pythonpath)) ``` Same fix applies to the watcher branch in `GatewayRunner` (watcher_env PYTHONPATH). Affected location: `gateway/run.py`, `_ensure_windows_gateway_venv_imports` (lines ~508-511 on latest `origin/main`) and the `GatewayRunner` watcher_env block (~line 11370).

signal.title: Windows: desktop self-update frequently fails — running hermes.exe locked (os error 32); needs staged update or self-shutdown before replace
signal.text: ## Summary On Windows, the desktop app's self-update frequently fails with file-lock errors (os error 32: another process is using the file) because the updater tries to replace **hermes.exe** and the venv files **while the app itself is still running**. ## Root cause The updater runs inside the running app (or a child of it) and attempts to replace: - `venv/Scripts/hermes.exe` (locked by the running process) - venv packages (locked by the loaded interpreter) Windows does not allow replacing a running executable, so the update aborts. This is not a network or permission issue — it is a **design flaw in the self-update flow**: it never shuts itself down (or defers the swap to a restart) before replacing files. ## Observed behavior - 'Update failed' toast/status repeatedly across 8/15, 8/17, 8/20 - Logs show `os error 32: 另一个程序正在使用此文件 (another program is using this file)` - Falling behind remote by ~33 commits at times because updates keep failing ## Every failed/successful update also leaves residue Each update attempt (successful or failed) drops a `state.db.pre-update-emergency-<timestamp>.bak` (~650-750MB each) and a `win-unpacked.bak` (~380MB) that are never cleaned up. After a few updates these accumulate to **2.5-3 GB** of junk. Recent 7-day C: drive growth attributable to Hermes updates alone: ~6.5 GB. ## Proposed fixes (any of) 1. **Staged/atomic update**: download new version to a temp dir, then on next app start (before the main process fully boots) swap files — the classic 'update on restart' pattern. 2. **Self-shutdown before replace**: updater asks the app to exit cleanly, waits for PID to die, then replaces files, then relaunches. 3. **Cleanup residue**: after a successful update, delete `state.db.pre-update-emergency-*.bak` and `win-unpacked.bak` automatically (or keep only the most recent one). ## Environment - Windows 10 19045 - Hermes desktop app, branch main - Venv-based install under `AppData/Local/hermes`
